+## 19.3 Qānūn-Map: a human-governed legal knowledge architecture
+Qānūn-Map is the proposed name for a linked legal knowledge and decision-support architecture. It is not a new legal order and, at the present stage, is not a deployed public system. Its purpose is to preserve the path from source to implementation in a form usable by lawyers, drafters, regulators, service designers, engineers, regulated persons and reviewers.
+The architecture contains seven connected stores or services:
+1. an **authoritative-source register** containing instruments, issuers, official locations, authentication evidence, dates, status and checksums;
+2. a **norm map** that divides instruments into addressable provisions and records definitions, powers, duties, exceptions, amendments, dependencies and conflicts;
+3. an **obligation model** expressing the actor, activity, condition, duty, exception, evidence, institution, decision, reason and remedy;
+4. an **evidence schema** defining what a supplied fact means, its source, custodian, quality, time and permissible use;
+5. a **test suite** containing ordinary cases, boundary cases, missing-input cases, conflicts, amendments and prohibited outcomes;
+6. a **decision-file service** that records the model and source version used, questions asked, inputs supplied, path, warnings, human officer, reasons and action; and
+7. a **review and change layer** for correction, appeal, legal update, regression testing, rollback, publication and audit.

+## 19.4 Normative hierarchy, source status and version control
+Qānūn-Map should encode authority before it encodes outcomes. That authority cannot be represented as one universal ladder in which every source simply ranks above or below every other. It must preserve several legal dimensions:

+|---|---|
+| constitutional supremacy | no statute, delegated instrument or administrative act may be treated as valid authority contrary to the Constitution as lawfully interpreted |
+| legislative competence | identify whether the matter and instrument are federal or provincial and apply the constitutional distribution and conflict rules; do not assume that one legislature’s Act universally ranks above the other’s |
+| delegated legislation | link each Rule, Regulation, notification or other instrument to its enabling Act, maker, procedure, Gazette status, scope and consistency limits; instrument names alone do not establish an inter se rank |
+| judicial authority | record court, bench, date, precedential status, issue and material factual setting; precedent operates through the judicial hierarchy and legal doctrine, not as another paragraph in a legislative stack |
+| administrative act | identify the statutory power, delegate, case, reasons and review status; an administrative decision may determine a case within power but is not equivalent to general legislation |
+| guidance and operations | label standards, circulars, forms, FAQs and internal instructions by their actual legal effect; publication in software does not promote them into binding law |

The official material checked for this report continued to distinguish the Act, NOC stage, draft VASP Regulations and prospective full licens

+| text | exact provision, language, official locator and any authorised correction |

+| integrity | file checksum, extraction method, reviewer and last verified date |
+| model link | rule objects, test suite, implementation version and release approval |
+The system should distinguish **source version**, **model version**, **engine version** and **service version**. A statute can remain unchanged while a faulty model is corrected. A model can remain unchanged while the evaluation engine changes. A service interface can change without altering either. Combining all four under “latest version” makes audit impossible.
+Updates must never be silent. A source change enters quarantine; a legal owner verifies authority and temporal effect; the model is amended in a separate branch; the full test suite runs; affected institutions approve within their functions; and a signed release states which cases may change. If urgent legal change precedes a tested model, the safe response is to suspend the affected automated ro
+Temporal logic deserves separate testing. Publication, commencement, transition, savings, repeal and retrospective effect are not interchangeable dates. A consolidated text may be convenient for present questions but may obscure the provision governing an earlier transaction. +## 19.5 A machine-readable obligation model
+The smallest useful Qānūn-Map object is not a paragraph of code. It is a legal proposition whose elements and consequences can be inspected independently. For a VASP-perimeter screen, the object may be expressed as follows:
+| Element | Structured representation | Human/legal boundary |
+|---|---|---|
+| actor | identified person; legal form; role; verified entity and representative identifiers | whether multiple actors form one service or exercise control |
+| activity | described function, customer journey, asset flow, custody, interface, remuneration and jurisdiction | classification by substance, function, use and economic effect |
+| territorial condition | carried on, or held out as carried on, in or from Pakistan | targeting, representations and cross-border facts may be disputed |
+| business condition | business and professional basis | isolated activity, group allocation and commercial substance require evidence |
+| relational condition | service to third parties | principal/agent, own-account and customer relationships require legal analysis |
+| service category | section 18 and Schedule I candidate category | ambiguous or combined services require reasoned classification |
+| exception/perimeter | section 2 exclusions and SBP/SECP or other connected law | no automatic exemption; competent regulator coordination may be required |
+| current legal proposition | the Act’s scope, VASP definition, service categories and NOC/licensing provisions apply according to their terms | exact NOC, licence, unauthorised-activity or transition consequence depends on operative law and proved facts |
+| recommended administrative routing | route a potentially in-scope case to PVARA without representing that the screen proves a licence, exemption or breach | this is a safe workflow recommendation, not a new statutory duty triggered merely by screening uncertainty |
+| evidence | terms, user flow, entity records, wallet/key control, fees, transaction samples and marketing | authenticity, completeness, privilege and weight remain reviewable |
+| institution | PVARA for VAA classification; connected institution for its own statutory perimeter | coordination does not transfer statutory competence |
+| reason/remedy | cited path, missing facts, decision-maker, review and appeal route | only the competent body can make the relevant order or adjudication |
+The Virtual Assets Act supplies the principal source chain. Section 2 states the Pakistan nexus and express exclusions. Section 3 defines a VASP as a person who, as a business, provides one or more virtual-asset services to third parties on a professional basis. Section 9(1)(f) authorises PVARA to classify by substance and economic effect, with consultation where SBP or SECP characteristics appea
+These provisions contain both formal and evaluative elements. Code can check that a declared entity identifier exists, that a date has a valid format, that required evidence fields are present, that a selected service category has a source link, or that two supplied Boolean values follow a declared branch. It cannot establish, merely from an applicant’s checkbox, that an operation is “professiona
+Accordingly, an automation model should classify functions by permitted use rather than by optimism about technical capability:
+- **publication and retrieval:** source discovery, provision linking and status display;
+- **syntactic validation:** format, completeness, arithmetic, date and identifier checks;
+- **screening and routing:** candidate classification and identification of the competent human pathway;
+- **decision support:** comparison of evidence with declared criteria, with an authorised officer independently responsible for reasons and result; and
+- **prohibited automatic consequence:** refusal, licence grant or variation, sanction, freeze, tax assessment, liability finding, merits determination or appeal disposition without the human authority and process required by law.
+Some calculations may be highly determinate yet still depend on human-controlled inputs. Even a deadline calculation requires the correct triggering event, communication date, governing version and any lawful extension. The calculation can be reproducible while the legal premise is contested. The output must therefore show both the answer and the assumptions on which it rests.
+Missing information should produce a typed state, not a guessed value. `UNKNOWN` means a fact was not supplied or verified. `[GAP]` means the governing source or institutional mechanism is absent or unresolved. `[DRAFT]` means the candidate rule lacks operative status. `CONFLICT` means two apparently applicable authorities or data sources cannot be reconciled. +## 19.7 Regulatory data, interoperability, privacy and evidence
+A rule model is only as reliable as its source and input data. Interoperability should therefore begin with identifiers and meaning, not bulk data transfer. The system needs stable identifiers for instruments, provisions, organisations, licences, permissions, officers, applications, evidence items, decisions, cases and model releases. Each shared field requires a definition, lawful purpose, sourc
+The Digital Nation Pakistan Act defines digital public infrastructure to include identity, data exchange, cloud and open-data components and gives the Pakistan Digital Authority important standards and coordination functions. It also preserves control and responsibility of designated data custodians and expressly requires avoidance of overlap with other regulatory mandates.[^452] That supports a
+The data architecture should use minimum disclosure. An eligibility or perimeter query often requires verification of a proposition rather than disclosure of the underlying record. A system may need to know that a company exists and that a representative holds a valid role, not retrieve every filing or personal identifier. Access should be role-based and purpose-limited; sensitive evidence should
+Chapter 12 established that data protection, cybersecurity and evidence are separate legal questions. A secure database can still be unlawful; a lawful collection can still be insecure; and an accurate system log can still require proof of attribution and integrity. Qānūn-Map should preserve the source of an input, who supplied or changed it, when it was valid, the method of verification and any
+Evidence exports must be intelligible without the live system. A decision file should contain the operative source text or stable official locator, all relevant versions, inputs, provenance, branch path, reasons, human approvals, notices and later changes in a durable format. Retention must follow legal purpose and proceedings, not the convenience of indefinite storage. A person should be able to
+Interoperability also requires graceful failure. If an identity, company, tax, sanctions or regulator interface is unavailable, the service should show the failure and offer a lawful alternative. “No response from another database” must not be translated into “not eligible” or “non-compliant”. Cross-agency APIs should carry status and timestamp, not just values, and each institution must remain r
+## 19.8 Human authority, explanation and contestability
+Human control is not satisfied by placing an officer after an automated result if the officer lacks time, evidence, training or authority to depart from it. Meaningful human judgment requires the power to ask for more information, change a classification, refuse the model’s recommendation, record reasons and trigger correction of a defective rule. The reviewer must know which parts were calculate
+The workflow must also guard against automation bias. A prominently displayed score or “recommended outcome” may become functionally decisive even when a form permits override. Assurance should therefore examine actual override rates, time available for review, whether officers receive the underlying evidence rather than only the output, and whether departures attract inappropriate managerial pre
+The Constitution requires public power to be exercised through law, fair process and legally responsible institutions. The VAA allocates classification and licensing functions to PVARA, requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage and provides an appellate structure for persons aggrieved by Authority orders.[^454] Software cannot become the statutory Authority, an appellate tribunal or t
+Every result that may affect a person should disclose:
+1. the purpose and non-binding or binding status of the process;
+2. the source instruments and exact versions used;
+3. the material facts supplied, retrieved or inferred;
+4. the rule path and calculations;
+5. missing information, conflicts, `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states;
+6. the responsible institution and named or identifiable decision function;
+7. the human reasons for any operative decision;
+8. how to correct facts, make representations and obtain the record; and
+9. the complaint, review, appeal or court route available under law.
+Explanation should track the actual decision. A generic statement that “requirements were not met” is not cured by attaching hundreds of rules. The officer should identify the decisive legal provision, factual finding, evidence accepted or rejected, treatment of a material representation and consequence selected. Where security or investigation law justifies withholding particular information, th
+No automated tool should make or execute an adverse legal decision merely because its prediction is accurate on historical data. Prediction and authority are different. Historical outcomes may encode inconsistent administration, exclusion or error. A machine-learning score may help prioritise a review only under an approved purpose and assurance regime; it should not supply an undisclosed substan
+Contestability also improves the model. Successful challenges, withdrawn decisions and unusual cases should enter the regression suite after legal review. +A remedy must remain usable outside the platform. Loss of an account, service outage or inaccessible interface cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or right to make representations. +Qānūn-Map requires institutional governance before scale. The minimum operating model separates five roles: the authoritative-source custodian; the legal-model owner; the responsible regulatory decision owner; the engineering and security owner; and an assurance function able to stop release. The same person or vendor should not authenticate the law, interpret it, write the implementation, approv

+|---|---|

+Change control should use dual approval by legal and technical owners. A source update triggers an impact report identifying affected rules, tests, services and prior cases. +Independent assurance should sample source pinpoints, reproduce results, challenge edge cases, inspect access and change logs, test the remedy and ask whether the system has become functionally mandatory despite being described as optional. +## 19.11 A phased demonstration programme—and the limit of execution
+The programme should advance by evidence gates, not by announcing a national platform and filling it later.
+**Phase 0 — source integrity.** Establish authenticated source registers for the VAA, valid subordinate instruments and directly connected law. Assign provision identifiers, status, commencement, amendment and official-location metadata. Publicly separate operative, draft, historical and missing material. No executable case outcome is required.
+**Phase 1 — controlled research prototype.** Refactor the existing perimeter screen into a self-contained, reproducible package. Replace legal-conclusion checkboxes with human determination objects. Add missing-input, draft, gap, cross-regulator and source-change cases. Publish the rule map, limitations and test results as research. Success is faithful traceability and safe escalation, not approv
+**Phase 2 — institutional shadow pilot.** With PVARA and connected institutions’ approval, trained officers run the model alongside—not inside—the live process. It cannot affect an applicant. Compare its questions and routing with human files; record disagreement; test privacy, security, accessibility and record export; and verify that the real review route works.
+**Phase 3 — legal validation.** Responsible institutions approve a bounded rule set, use, version and reasons protocol through the appropriate legal and administrative instruments. Independent reviewers test authority, source fidelity, edge cases, data and prohibited outcomes. Any `[GAP]` that controls the result prevents progression.
+**Phase 4 — bounded public assistance and scale decision.** A public service may explain the perimeter, collect an evidence inventory and route a user to the competent process. It should not issue a compliance badge or licence. Scale occurs only after measured reduction in error or burden, no material rights or security defect, demonstrable human override, working remedies, sustainable ownership
+The stop rules are as important as the phases. Code must never decide whether Parliament conferred a power; resolve an unresolved conflict between statutes; determine a contested legal character solely from a label; find dishonesty or liability; impose a sanction; freeze property; grant, refuse, suspend or revoke a licence; decide proportionality; dispose of an appeal; or prevent a court from exa
+This boundary is not hostility to technology. It is the condition for trustworthy technology in public law. **Code** supplies precision, reproducibility and the capacity to test implementation. **Law** supplies authority, rights, limits, reasons and remedy. **Capital** supplies capability and exposure: the resources to build systems, the incentives that may distort them, and the losses distribute
+Pakistan’s contribution need not be the largest automated regulatory platform. It can be more important: a model of machine-legible administration in which the source is authenticated, drafts cannot masquerade as law, gaps stop false certainty, every branch is traceable, institutions retain their lawful competence, adverse decisions remain reasoned and reviewable, and correction improves both tex

Chapter 19 — From National Digital Masterplan to Machine-Executable Regulation

> Status and evidence cut-off. Substantive working draft for Author review. The current-status propositions made here were checked against the identified official materials as at 16 August 2026; this is not a claim of an exhaustive whole-field status census, and the reading scope and unresolved release checks are recorded in the Chapter 19 source-and-status record. Qānūn-Map is a proposed research architecture. The VASP activity-perimeter material examined in this chapter is an existing research demonstration, not an official PVARA instrument, regulatory decision, licence-readiness service or component of the National Digital Masterplan. No machine-readable representation displaces the authenticated Gazette text, valid delegated legislation, a competent human decision or a lawful remedy.

19.1 The implementation problem: five things that must not be collapsed

Pakistan’s digital-assets problem is no longer the absence of a primary statute. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 supplies an operative authority, perimeter, licensing architecture, direct duties, enforcement powers, delegated-law structure and appeal pathway. The harder problem is implementation across five different objects: law, policy, administrative process, data and code. A statute states legal authority and obligations. Policy selects objectives. A process allocates work and decision points. Data records facts or claims about facts. Code performs defined operations on supplied inputs. A system becomes unsafe when it treats one object as proof of another.

A scanned Act is digital but not structured. Structured text is searchable but not necessarily machine-readable at provision level. A machine-readable provision is not necessarily executable. Executable logic is not necessarily legally correct. A technically correct implementation of a rule may still be used by an institution without power, applied to the wrong legal version, fed incomplete evidence, or allowed to produce a result that only a human officer or tribunal can lawfully decide.

Those errors have different owners and remedies. A drafting ambiguity may require an amending instrument. A mistaken model requires legal correction and regression testing. Poor evidence requires verification or a finding that the fact is not proved. An unauthorised decision requires institutional and legal redress even if the calculation was flawless. Treating every failure as an “IT issue” conceals the public body responsible for correcting it.

The target is therefore not “law replaced by software”. It is a governed chain from authenticated legal source to a transparent model, bounded test, reasoned administrative file and reviewable human act. Computation can expose contradiction, ask consistent questions, validate dates or document fields, reproduce a formula and route a case. It can also reveal where the law is incomplete or depends on judgment. It must not convert that incompleteness into an invented rule.

Chapter 18 handed forward an anticipatory dashboard. Every indicator required a stable identifier, source, status, version, evidence, responsible institution, lawful action, reason, safeguard, remedy and review date. This chapter turns that requirement into an architecture. Its controlling rule is simple: the official legal instrument authorises; the model represents; the program assists; the competent person decides where law or fact requires judgment.

AML/CFT, Travel Rule and sanctions allocationactor, threshold, message, exception, evidence and protected-route objectsdraft thresholds and private network rules cannot become present law
tax taxonomy and reportingevent, taxpayer, timing, value, source, basis and uncertainty fieldscalculation does not create a tax charge or settle a contested classification
Tribunal, reasons and remedy packagedecision owner, reasons, notice, record and review-route objectssoftware cannot become the Authority, Tribunal or court
National Digital Masterplan sectoral alignmentinstitutional owner, dependency, milestone and assurance metadataplanning architecture cannot confer another body's coercive power

The table is a lineage control, not a new reform programme. Chapter 19 tests whether selected Chapter 17 obligations can be represented accurately and safely; it does not displace the diagnosis, legal vehicle, institutional owner, reasons or remedy already identified.

19.2 Law as Code, Rules as Code and the authority boundary

“Law as Code” and “Rules as Code” are useful only if their meanings are separated. Law as Code is the broader inquiry into how legal norms can be represented, tested or implemented computationally and how code itself structures conduct. Rules as Code is a public-administration method: selected rules are expressed in machine-consumable form, ideally through a multidisciplinary process connected to policy and legislative drafting. Neither phrase establishes that software is law.

Four artefacts may coexist:

ArtefactWhat it doesWhat it cannot prove
authenticated human-readable instrumentstates the enacted or validly made rule in its authoritative formthat an administrative or software implementation is correct
structured legal representationidentifies provisions, definitions, amendments, relationships and metadatathat every provision is reducible to determinate logic
executable modelapplies declared conditions, calculations or routes to supplied inputslegal truth of contested inputs, institutional competence or lawful exercise of discretion
service implementationcollects evidence, calls the model, records action and communicates with a userauthority beyond the governing law or immunity from reasons, review and remedy

The OECD’s 2020 working paper describes Rules as Code as an official machine-consumable version produced alongside human-readable rules and treats it as a change in rulemaking, not merely a software project. It also records limitations and competing conceptions rather than presenting one mature global standard.446 New Zealand’s Better Rules discovery similarly used multidisciplinary teams and tested concept models, decision models and rule statements. Its important negative finding was that not all legislation is suitable for machine consumption.447 These are comparative foundations, not sources of Pakistani authority.

The distinction between machine-readable, machine-consumable and machine-executable should be maintained. A provision with a stable identifier, dates and subject tags is machine-readable. A structured obligation that a service can query is machine-consumable. A rule that evaluates inputs and returns a result is executable. Each transition adds interpretation and therefore adds a new point at which error, institutional bias or silent legal change can enter.

The terms describe capability, not authority.

Standardised identifiers and metadata can improve access without purporting to decide cases. The European Legislation Identifier, for example, uses persistent identifiers and structured metadata so legislation can be accessed, exchanged and reused across systems.448 Pakistan can learn from that publication architecture without importing European law or assuming that linked data resolves statutory interpretation.

Three propositions follow.

First, official status is a legal question. A government-hosted file may be a consultation draft, guidance, a consolidated convenience copy or an operative instrument. A machine must carry that status, not infer authority from a domain name. Secondly, equivalence between text and model cannot be self-declared by the developer. It requires legal mapping, test cases and approval within the relevant institution’s competence. Thirdly, even an officially published computational model would require an express rule about its legal effect. Until Parliament or valid delegated legislation says otherwise, the authenticated legal text and competent decision remain controlling.

This report therefore uses a deliberately bounded formulation: Qānūn-Map may make legal requirements more legible, traceable and testable. It does not make public power self-executing. “Code is law” is rejected both descriptively and constitutionally. Code can constrain a workflow, but only law can supply the State’s authority to burden a person, and only an authorised process can turn proved facts into an adverse public decision.

19.3 Qānūn-Map: a human-governed legal knowledge architecture

Qānūn-Map is the proposed name for a linked legal knowledge and decision-support architecture. It is not a new legal order and, at the present stage, is not a deployed public system. Its purpose is to preserve the path from source to implementation in a form usable by lawyers, drafters, regulators, service designers, engineers, regulated persons and reviewers.

The architecture contains seven connected stores or services:

1. an authoritative-source register containing instruments, issuers, official locations, authentication evidence, dates, status and checksums;

2. a norm map that divides instruments into addressable provisions and records definitions, powers, duties, exceptions, amendments, dependencies and conflicts;

3. an obligation model expressing the actor, activity, condition, duty, exception, evidence, institution, decision, reason and remedy;

4. an evidence schema defining what a supplied fact means, its source, custodian, quality, time and permissible use;

5. a test suite containing ordinary cases, boundary cases, missing-input cases, conflicts, amendments and prohibited outcomes;

6. a decision-file service that records the model and source version used, questions asked, inputs supplied, path, warnings, human officer, reasons and action; and

7. a review and change layer for correction, appeal, legal update, regression testing, rollback, publication and audit.

Figure 19.1 — From legal text to a reviewable Qānūn-Map

```mermaid

flowchart LR

A["Authenticated Gazette instrument"] --> B["Provision and metadata register"]

B --> C["Lawyer-drafter norm map"]

C --> D["Structured obligation and evidence model"]

D --> E["Executable tests and routing"]

E --> F["Human decision file"]

F --> G["Reasons, notice and remedy"]
```

Source note: Author’s architecture derived from the Pakistani hierarchy and Chapters 12–18, informed comparatively by OECD Rules as Code, New Zealand Better Rules and the European Legislation Identifier. The arrows show provenance and governance, not a transfer of legal authority to code.

The architecture must allow movement in both directions. An amendment flows from source registration through remapping and testing before release. An appeal or operational incident flows backwards: the reviewer can reconstruct the source, model, inputs and human act, identify whether the defect was legal, factual, technical or procedural, and correct the appropriate layer. A system that stores only the final output cannot support that inquiry.

Qānūn-Map also separates a legal model from an administrative business rule. A statute may require an application “in such form and manner” as prescribed. A regulator may validly prescribe fields. An office may then adopt internal routing, file-naming and workload practices. Those layers have different authority. Internal convenience must not become an undisclosed condition of eligibility, and a technical validation must not reject an application because a non-statutory preference was coded as mandatory.

Every rule object should be readable by a lawyer without executing software. At minimum it should display its plain-language proposition, exact source locator, status, effective period, institution, input definition, output meaning, escalation condition, test results and change history. Open publication is preferred for general legal models and test cases, subject to security, privacy, investigative secrecy and intellectual-property constraints lawfully identified. The public should be able to see why the model asks a question and what it will not decide.

Two labels are essential. `[DRAFT]` means text or logic exists but is not operative authority. It may be used in a sandbox or policy simulation only if every screen and output preserves that status and segregates it from live decisions. `[GAP]` means a required source, rule, fact, institutional assignment or remedy has not been verified. A gap is not permission for the developer to select the most convenient answer. In an operative pathway, either label must stop the affected conclusion and route the matter to an authorised human process.

19.4 Normative hierarchy, source status and version control

Qānūn-Map should encode authority before it encodes outcomes. That authority cannot be represented as one universal ladder in which every source simply ranks above or below every other. It must preserve several legal dimensions:

Authority dimensionRule for the model
constitutional supremacyno statute, delegated instrument or administrative act may be treated as valid authority contrary to the Constitution as lawfully interpreted
legislative competenceidentify whether the matter and instrument are federal or provincial and apply the constitutional distribution and conflict rules; do not assume that one legislature’s Act universally ranks above the other’s
delegated legislationlink each Rule, Regulation, notification or other instrument to its enabling Act, maker, procedure, Gazette status, scope and consistency limits; instrument names alone do not establish an inter se rank
judicial authorityrecord court, bench, date, precedential status, issue and material factual setting; precedent operates through the judicial hierarchy and legal doctrine, not as another paragraph in a legislative stack
administrative actidentify the statutory power, delegate, case, reasons and review status; an administrative decision may determine a case within power but is not equivalent to general legislation
guidance and operationslabel standards, circulars, forms, FAQs and internal instructions by their actual legal effect; publication in software does not promote them into binding law

The Virtual Assets Act illustrates why this matters. The Act came into force at once and authorises federal Rules by Gazette notification and PVARA Regulations through the statutory procedure. Its direct provisions coexist with matters left to prescription. The official material checked for this report continued to distinguish the Act, NOC stage, draft VASP Regulations and prospective full licensing.449 A model may use an operative statutory proposition where its elements are sufficiently clear. It must not fill a prescribed-detail gap from a consultation draft and then label the result current law.

Every source object should contain at least:

FieldRequired content
identityjurisdiction, instrument type, official title, number and stable provision ID
authorityissuing body, enabling provision and authentication evidence
status`OPERATIVE_VERIFIED`, `[DRAFT]`, `[GAP]`, `HISTORICAL`, `SUPERSEDED`, `SUSPENDED` or `NOT_READ`
timemaking, publication, commencement, effective-from, effective-to and transition dates
textexact provision, language, official locator and any authorised correction
relationshipamends, repeals, saves, overrides, depends on, conflicts with or implements
integrityfile checksum, extraction method, reviewer and last verified date
model linkrule objects, test suite, implementation version and release approval

The system should distinguish source version, model version, engine version and service version. A statute can remain unchanged while a faulty model is corrected. A model can remain unchanged while the evaluation engine changes. A service interface can change without altering either. Combining all four under “latest version” makes audit impossible.

Updates must never be silent. A source change enters quarantine; a legal owner verifies authority and temporal effect; the model is amended in a separate branch; the full test suite runs; affected institutions approve within their functions; and a signed release states which cases may change. If urgent legal change precedes a tested model, the safe response is to suspend the affected automated route and use a human process under the new law. Continuing to run a known superseded model for convenience is not digital continuity; it is systematic legal error.

Temporal logic deserves separate testing. Publication, commencement, transition, savings, repeal and retrospective effect are not interchangeable dates. A consolidated text may be convenient for present questions but may obscure the provision governing an earlier transaction. The decision file must preserve the version applied to the relevant event and the legal reason for applying it. Where a court has interpreted a provision, the model should link the decision and its precedential status without converting a fact-sensitive holding into a universal Boolean rule.

19.5 A machine-readable obligation model

The smallest useful Qānūn-Map object is not a paragraph of code. It is a legal proposition whose elements and consequences can be inspected independently. For a VASP-perimeter screen, the object may be expressed as follows:

ElementStructured representationHuman/legal boundary
actoridentified person; legal form; role; verified entity and representative identifierswhether multiple actors form one service or exercise control
activitydescribed function, customer journey, asset flow, custody, interface, remuneration and jurisdictionclassification by substance, function, use and economic effect
territorial conditioncarried on, or held out as carried on, in or from Pakistantargeting, representations and cross-border facts may be disputed
business conditionbusiness and professional basisisolated activity, group allocation and commercial substance require evidence
relational conditionservice to third partiesprincipal/agent, own-account and customer relationships require legal analysis
service categorysection 18 and Schedule I candidate categoryambiguous or combined services require reasoned classification
exception/perimetersection 2 exclusions and SBP/SECP or other connected lawno automatic exemption; competent regulator coordination may be required
current legal propositionthe Act’s scope, VASP definition, service categories and NOC/licensing provisions apply according to their termsexact NOC, licence, unauthorised-activity or transition consequence depends on operative law and proved facts
recommended administrative routingroute a potentially in-scope case to PVARA without representing that the screen proves a licence, exemption or breachthis is a safe workflow recommendation, not a new statutory duty triggered merely by screening uncertainty
evidenceterms, user flow, entity records, wallet/key control, fees, transaction samples and marketingauthenticity, completeness, privilege and weight remain reviewable
institutionPVARA for VAA classification; connected institution for its own statutory perimetercoordination does not transfer statutory competence
reason/remedycited path, missing facts, decision-maker, review and appeal routeonly the competent body can make the relevant order or adjudication

The Virtual Assets Act supplies the principal source chain. Section 2 states the Pakistan nexus and express exclusions. Section 3 defines a VASP as a person who, as a business, provides one or more virtual-asset services to third parties on a professional basis. Section 9(1)(f) authorises PVARA to classify by substance and economic effect, with consultation where SBP or SECP characteristics appear. Section 18 and Schedule I identify service categories. Section 19 then begins the NOC and licence application sequence and requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage.450

These provisions contain both formal and evaluative elements. Code can check that a declared entity identifier exists, that a date has a valid format, that required evidence fields are present, that a selected service category has a source link, or that two supplied Boolean values follow a declared branch. It cannot establish, merely from an applicant’s checkbox, that an operation is “professional”, that a software arrangement is truly own-account, that a token is excluded, or that no securities, payments, foreign-exchange or deposit-taking perimeter is engaged.

Accordingly, an automation model should classify functions by permitted use rather than by optimism about technical capability:

  • publication and retrieval: source discovery, provision linking and status display;
  • syntactic validation: format, completeness, arithmetic, date and identifier checks;
  • screening and routing: candidate classification and identification of the competent human pathway;
  • decision support: comparison of evidence with declared criteria, with an authorised officer independently responsible for reasons and result; and
  • prohibited automatic consequence: refusal, licence grant or variation, sanction, freeze, tax assessment, liability finding, merits determination or appeal disposition without the human authority and process required by law.

Some calculations may be highly determinate yet still depend on human-controlled inputs. Even a deadline calculation requires the correct triggering event, communication date, governing version and any lawful extension. The calculation can be reproducible while the legal premise is contested. The output must therefore show both the answer and the assumptions on which it rests.

Missing information should produce a typed state, not a guessed value. `UNKNOWN` means a fact was not supplied or verified. `[GAP]` means the governing source or institutional mechanism is absent or unresolved. `[DRAFT]` means the candidate rule lacks operative status. `CONFLICT` means two apparently applicable authorities or data sources cannot be reconciled. Each state should generate the responsible owner and next lawful action. None should default to refusal.

19.6 Demonstration: the VASP activity-perimeter screen

The project contains a VASP activity-perimeter demonstrator. This chapter does not present it as a regulator product or licence-readiness tool. It is a research artefact with a JSON rule map, three input cases, a runner and saved results. Its declared version is `0.1.0-demo`; its declared status is `research_demo`; and its notice states that the Gazette remains authoritative, that PVARA and other competent regulators retain authority, and that no licence or legal conclusion is produced automatically.451 The last phrase is imprecise because the outputs do express tentative screening conclusions. The accurate boundary is that the demonstrator produces no final, binding or statutory legal determination.

The map asks six questions in sequence: Pakistan nexus; professional business basis; service to third parties; apparent Schedule I match; absence of an identified express exclusion; and absence of an unresolved connected-regulator issue. Its metadata marks every node as requiring human control, but does not define the required role. A controlled redesign should distinguish user assertions, clerical authentication, legally qualified classification, connected-regulator concurrence, override authority and the final statutory decision. The terminal branches either say that a proposition has not been established on the supplied facts or route the matter for human classification. Even the most positive branch says only “potential VASP route to PVARA”.

On 16 August 2026 the saved runner was executed against the three saved cases. The generated results had the same SHA-256 checksum before and after execution. That establishes reproducibility of this particular run in the checked environment; it does not validate the legal model, underlying facts or deployment architecture.

Test caseSupplied issueReproduced path outcomeWhat remains human
D1 — custodial walletall six supplied predicates marked true`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; potential VASP route to PVARAsource authentication, factual proof, classification, NOC/licensing stage and connected permissions
D2 — ambiguous software providerSchedule I match marked false`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; service classification requiredwhether software, interface, custody, execution, control or remuneration constitutes a listed service
D3 — fiat-referenced payment tokenconnected-perimeter conflict marked unresolved`ESCALATE_HUMAN`; interagency classification requiredPVARA, SBP, SECP or other competence, payment/FX treatment and applicable entry route

The demonstration proves only a narrow technical proposition: a defined tree can take supplied values, follow a repeatable path, return a reason code and preserve cited provenance. It does not prove that the model contains every relevant provision; that each supplied value is true; that the cited extract is the latest authoritative text; that the engine is secure; that the tool can authenticate evidence; or that a regulator has approved the labels, automation classes or outcomes.

The label “licence readiness” must also be used carefully. The existing map is an activity-perimeter screen. It does not test incorporation, NOC documentation, controllers, key individuals, fit-and-proper criteria, capital, customer assets, AML/CFT, technology, governance, outsourcing, business continuity, complaints or wind-down. A future readiness module would need a separate, status-controlled obligation set derived from operative requirements. Where required details remain in `[DRAFT]` regulations or are `[GAP]`, the system may prepare an evidence inventory or simulate proposed requirements, but it cannot present readiness as legal compliance.

19.7 Regulatory data, interoperability, privacy and evidence

A rule model is only as reliable as its source and input data. Interoperability should therefore begin with identifiers and meaning, not bulk data transfer. The system needs stable identifiers for instruments, provisions, organisations, licences, permissions, officers, applications, evidence items, decisions, cases and model releases. Each shared field requires a definition, lawful purpose, source custodian, validation rule, time quality and correction route.

The Digital Nation Pakistan Act defines digital public infrastructure to include identity, data exchange, cloud and open-data components and gives the Pakistan Digital Authority important standards and coordination functions. It also preserves control and responsibility of designated data custodians and expressly requires avoidance of overlap with other regulatory mandates.452 That supports a common technical layer; it does not create permission for PVARA, PDA or a vendor to collect or combine any dataset that would be useful.

The data architecture should use minimum disclosure. An eligibility or perimeter query often requires verification of a proposition rather than disclosure of the underlying record. A system may need to know that a company exists and that a representative holds a valid role, not retrieve every filing or personal identifier. Access should be role-based and purpose-limited; sensitive evidence should be encrypted, logged and segregated; test data should be synthetic or lawfully de-identified; and public rule models should not expose investigative thresholds whose disclosure would defeat a lawful function.

Chapter 12 established that data protection, cybersecurity and evidence are separate legal questions. A secure database can still be unlawful; a lawful collection can still be insecure; and an accurate system log can still require proof of attribution and integrity. Qānūn-Map should preserve the source of an input, who supplied or changed it, when it was valid, the method of verification and any contest. Hashes and digital signatures can assist integrity and authentication, but they cannot prove that the original factual assertion was true.453

Evidence exports must be intelligible without the live system. A decision file should contain the operative source text or stable official locator, all relevant versions, inputs, provenance, branch path, reasons, human approvals, notices and later changes in a durable format. Retention must follow legal purpose and proceedings, not the convenience of indefinite storage. A person should be able to correct an erroneous factual record without rewriting the historical fact that the earlier decision used it.

Interoperability also requires graceful failure. If an identity, company, tax, sanctions or regulator interface is unavailable, the service should show the failure and offer a lawful alternative. “No response from another database” must not be translated into “not eligible” or “non-compliant”. Cross-agency APIs should carry status and timestamp, not just values, and each institution must remain responsible for the field it authoritatively maintains.

19.8 Human authority, explanation and contestability

Human control is not satisfied by placing an officer after an automated result if the officer lacks time, evidence, training or authority to depart from it. Meaningful human judgment requires the power to ask for more information, change a classification, refuse the model’s recommendation, record reasons and trigger correction of a defective rule. The reviewer must know which parts were calculated and which were legal or factual assumptions.

The workflow must also guard against automation bias. A prominently displayed score or “recommended outcome” may become functionally decisive even when a form permits override. Assurance should therefore examine actual override rates, time available for review, whether officers receive the underlying evidence rather than only the output, and whether departures attract inappropriate managerial pressure. For contested or adverse cases, the interface should present the legal question and evidence before any system recommendation, so that the officer forms an independent view.

The Constitution requires public power to be exercised through law, fair process and legally responsible institutions. The VAA allocates classification and licensing functions to PVARA, requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage and provides an appellate structure for persons aggrieved by Authority orders.454 Software cannot become the statutory Authority, an appellate tribunal or the Supreme Court. Nor can a generic “human in the loop” transfer one regulator’s power to another institution.

Every result that may affect a person should disclose:

1. the purpose and non-binding or binding status of the process;

2. the source instruments and exact versions used;

3. the material facts supplied, retrieved or inferred;

4. the rule path and calculations;

5. missing information, conflicts, `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states;

6. the responsible institution and named or identifiable decision function;

7. the human reasons for any operative decision;

8. how to correct facts, make representations and obtain the record; and

9. the complaint, review, appeal or court route available under law.

Explanation should track the actual decision. A generic statement that “requirements were not met” is not cured by attaching hundreds of rules. The officer should identify the decisive legal provision, factual finding, evidence accepted or rejected, treatment of a material representation and consequence selected. Where security or investigation law justifies withholding particular information, the limitation itself needs authority and review; secrecy should not become the default explanation for system opacity.

No automated tool should make or execute an adverse legal decision merely because its prediction is accurate on historical data. Prediction and authority are different. Historical outcomes may encode inconsistent administration, exclusion or error. A machine-learning score may help prioritise a review only under an approved purpose and assurance regime; it should not supply an undisclosed substantive criterion. For the bounded programme proposed here, the preferable core is transparent deterministic logic, with analytics kept separate and never allowed to overwrite the legal rule path.

Contestability also improves the model. Successful challenges, withdrawn decisions and unusual cases should enter the regression suite after legal review. That does not mean that a single officer’s decision rewrites the law. It means the programme tests whether the model omitted an exception, misrepresented an ambiguity, relied on poor data or invited users to answer a legal conclusion as if it were a simple fact.

A remedy must remain usable outside the platform. Loss of an account, service outage or inaccessible interface cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or right to make representations. Notices should identify an alternative channel, and the complete record should be obtainable in a durable human-readable form. The reviewing institution should be able to suspend reliance on a disputed model without disabling the underlying legal process.

19.9 Governance, assurance and controlled change

Qānūn-Map requires institutional governance before scale. The minimum operating model separates five roles: the authoritative-source custodian; the legal-model owner; the responsible regulatory decision owner; the engineering and security owner; and an assurance function able to stop release. The same person or vendor should not authenticate the law, interpret it, write the implementation, approve it and certify the result.

Each model release should pass six gates:

GateRequired proof
sourceauthenticated instrument, status, dates, hierarchy and amendment check
legal mappingprovision-by-provision derivation, unresolved interpretations and competent owner
datadefinitions, lawful access, provenance, correction, quality and privacy assessment
technicalreviewed code, pinned dependencies, security tests, reproducible build and rollback
casesordinary, boundary, missing, conflict, draft, gap, adversarial and prohibited-outcome tests
administrativeauthorised use, trained officer, reasons template, notice, record and working remedy

The inspected demonstrator also supplies five concrete pre-pilot defects for those gates. Its engine is imported from another research workspace and must be pinned, reviewed and hashed within an approved build. Its exclusion and connected-perimeter inputs are Boolean values although they are legal conclusions requiring an identified officer, evidence, reasons and validity period. Its exclusion predicate cites sections 3 and 5 although the principal express exclusions appear in section 2(2), so the map must be corrected and regression-tested. Its generic `hcc_required` flag does not allocate user, clerical, legal, inter-regulator, override and final-decision roles. Its notice should distinguish tentative screening output from a final, binding or statutory legal determination.

The test suite is a legal-control asset. It should include cases in which the correct output is “unknown”, “wrong institution”, “draft only”, “source conflict”, “human classification”, “insufficient authority” or “do not proceed”. A system tested only on clear approvals will predictably treat ambiguity as approval. A system tested only on enforcement cases will over-route ordinary activity as risk.

Change control should use dual approval by legal and technical owners. A source update triggers an impact report identifying affected rules, tests, services and prior cases. Material changes require notice and, where rights or duties change, the legal process required for the underlying instrument—not only a software release. Rollback must restore the last approved model and preserve decisions already taken for review. The audit log must include rejected releases and emergency overrides.

Procurement cannot outsource responsibility. A contract should require open data and rule formats where lawful, documentation, source and dependency disclosure, portability, security obligations, incident notice, audit access, exit assistance and continued access to decision records. Proprietary code must not prevent PVARA, a tribunal or a court from understanding the basis of a public decision. Vendor performance claims and laboratory accuracy are not evidence of lawful deployment.

Governance should include conflicts and participation. Regulated firms may properly test whether a rule model reflects operational reality, but they should not control the interpretation, acceptance tests or release decision for requirements that bind them. Applicants, customers, affected communities, lawyers, accessibility specialists and frontline officers should be able to expose burdens and edge cases through a recorded process. Consultation evidence should be published or summarised with reasons, while confidential and security-sensitive material remains protected under identified authority.

Independent assurance should sample source pinpoints, reproduce results, challenge edge cases, inspect access and change logs, test the remedy and ask whether the system has become functionally mandatory despite being described as optional. Material incidents include not only cyber compromise but use of a draft as operative law, a stale model, inability to explain a result, systematic override by staff, data drift, inaccessible review and any automatic adverse consequence outside authority.

Programme metrics should measure legal and administrative quality: source defects found, unresolved gaps, disagreement categories, corrected inputs, time and cost to complete the lawful process, successful challenges, security events and remedy availability. A high number of automated completions is not success if people cannot understand or contest them. The assurance function should report residual defects and have a defined suspension threshold.

19.10 National Digital Masterplan integration and institutional ownership

The Digital Nation Pakistan Act provides the planning and coordination setting for a future programme. The National Digital Commission approves the Masterplan and provides strategic direction. The Pakistan Digital Authority develops, implements, monitors and periodically updates it; coordinates across governments and regulators; develops technology standards and reference architectures; and monitors alignment. The Act requires sectoral and implementation plans, consultation, milestones and annual review.455

That framework can supply the horizontal layer: source and metadata standards, reference architecture, identity and data-exchange conventions, accessibility, cloud and security baselines, procurement patterns and programme monitoring. It does not make PDA the VAA decision-maker. Section 8(g) itself requires avoidance of overlap and conflict with other regulatory mandates. PVARA remains the vertical legal owner of VAA perimeter, licensing and supervision; SBP, SECP, FMU, FBR and other institutions remain owners of their respective law.

The institutional design should be recorded in the relevant sectoral and implementation plan, with budget, staff, milestones, risks, assurance and public outcome measures. A technical reference architecture without these owners would repeat the implementation gap the Masterplan is intended to address.

FunctionProposed accountable ownerBoundary
cross-government legal-data and service standardPDA under an approved Masterplan/valid instrumenttechnical coordination; no sector decision transfer
VAA source and obligation modelPVARA legal owner with Gazette/source custodian supportonly operative VAA material may drive live use
connected financial perimetereach competent regulator, through a recorded coordination processconcurrence or referral does not erase statutory competence
model engineering and operationapproved public team or procured supplier under institutional controlsupplier does not own legal interpretation or public decision
assurancefunctionally independent legal, technical, security and administrative reviewersauthority to stop or suspend release
public reportingPDA for programme indicators; each regulator for decisions and outcomes within its lawaggregated reporting must preserve privacy and legal status

Before an institutional shadow pilot and again before scale, a capacity-and-value gate should test whether the service improves rather than duplicates administration. The baseline should record current processing time, error and rework categories, officer time, unresolved referrals, applicant burden and cost. The pilot should identify which clerical or deterministic tasks it can actually complete, the expected percentage and volume of human escalations, required legal and technical staffing, source-maintenance cost, service levels and operating cost per case. If nearly every case receives another full review, the system adds delay without reducing legal risk. The programme should then narrow the use case, redesign it or stop. Progress requires an adopted benefit threshold and a termination rule, not an assumption that more digitisation equals more capacity.

At the evidence cut-off, the official National Digital Masterplan material reviewed by this report evidenced consultation and roadmap development, not an approved digital-assets Rules-as-Code sector plan.456 The proposed programme must therefore be described as a recommendation for possible inclusion through the Act’s approval and consultation process. Neither this report nor its demonstrator is the Masterplan.

Section 28 of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act also requires care. Its override provision preserves stronger data-rights and cybersecurity measures, and persistent conflicts are to be addressed through consultation, Commission action within law or proposed legislative amendment. It is not a machine rule allowing a shared platform to select the “higher” institutional mandate or transfer PVARA, SBP, SECP, FBR or judicial powers to PDA.457

19.11 A phased demonstration programme—and the limit of execution

The programme should advance by evidence gates, not by announcing a national platform and filling it later.

Phase 0 — source integrity. Establish authenticated source registers for the VAA, valid subordinate instruments and directly connected law. Assign provision identifiers, status, commencement, amendment and official-location metadata. Publicly separate operative, draft, historical and missing material. No executable case outcome is required.

Phase 1 — controlled research prototype. Refactor the existing perimeter screen into a self-contained, reproducible package. Replace legal-conclusion checkboxes with human determination objects. Add missing-input, draft, gap, cross-regulator and source-change cases. Publish the rule map, limitations and test results as research. Success is faithful traceability and safe escalation, not approval accuracy.

Phase 2 — institutional shadow pilot. With PVARA and connected institutions’ approval, trained officers run the model alongside—not inside—the live process. It cannot affect an applicant. Compare its questions and routing with human files; record disagreement; test privacy, security, accessibility and record export; and verify that the real review route works.

Phase 3 — legal validation. Responsible institutions approve a bounded rule set, use, version and reasons protocol through the appropriate legal and administrative instruments. Independent reviewers test authority, source fidelity, edge cases, data and prohibited outcomes. Any `[GAP]` that controls the result prevents progression.

Phase 4 — bounded public assistance and scale decision. A public service may explain the perimeter, collect an evidence inventory and route a user to the competent process. It should not issue a compliance badge or licence. Scale occurs only after measured reduction in error or burden, no material rights or security defect, demonstrable human override, working remedies, sustainable ownership and a reasoned Commission/sector decision under existing law.

The stop rules are as important as the phases. Code must never decide whether Parliament conferred a power; resolve an unresolved conflict between statutes; determine a contested legal character solely from a label; find dishonesty or liability; impose a sanction; freeze property; grant, refuse, suspend or revoke a licence; decide proportionality; dispose of an appeal; or prevent a court from examining legality. It may assemble the record, identify the question, calculate a formally determinate element, display alternatives and expose missing proof. The judgment and legal act remain with the authorised human institution.

This boundary is not hostility to technology. It is the condition for trustworthy technology in public law. Code supplies precision, reproducibility and the capacity to test implementation. Law supplies authority, rights, limits, reasons and remedy. Capital supplies capability and exposure: the resources to build systems, the incentives that may distort them, and the losses distributed when they fail. Intelligent order is achieved when each is made visible to the others without being allowed to impersonate them.

Pakistan’s contribution need not be the largest automated regulatory platform. It can be more important: a model of machine-legible administration in which the source is authenticated, drafts cannot masquerade as law, gaps stop false certainty, every branch is traceable, institutions retain their lawful competence, adverse decisions remain reasoned and reviewable, and correction improves both text and implementation. That is how a National Digital Masterplan can move toward machine-executable regulation without making regulation machine-sovereign.

Chapter 19 — Future: Scenarios and Anticipatory Legal Intelligence

> Status and evidence cut-off. Substantive working draft for Author review. Legal and institutional status is checked to 16 August 2026. The scenarios are conditional tests, not forecasts, probabilities, price projections or claims that any technology, market structure or reform will occur.

19.1 Scenario method, horizon and uncertainty

The purpose of foresight in this report is not to predict which token will succeed, how many Pakistanis will use a wallet, or when a global market cycle will turn. Its purpose is to expose decisions that become dangerous if they are first considered during a run, a failure, a constitutional challenge or a rapid shift in market structure. Chapter 18 supplied the corrective package. Chapter 19 asks whether that package remains usable when plausible conditions diverge from the assumptions under which it was drafted.

The scenarios use two planning horizons measured from a formally adopted implementation start. The operational horizon covers the period in which legal instruments, licensing, interfaces, supervisory systems and remedies are being made functional. The structural horizon covers the later period in which scale, concentration, new technical forms or changed international standards may test the architecture. These are not statutory deadlines. No probability is assigned, and no scenario is selected as the “expected” future.

Each scenario is constructed from seven elements:

1. an explicit assumption about market, technology or institutional conditions;

2. the law, institution or operational dependency placed under stress;

3. the mechanism by which the system could fail or produce unequal loss;

4. the persons, rights, assets and public interests affected;

5. safeguards already present in law or proposed in Chapter 18;

6. the residual risk after those safeguards; and

7. an observable indicator that should trigger review before the failure becomes acute.

The stress ratings used below describe consequence if the scenario occurs, not likelihood. “Low” means the stress is secondary and contained by ordinary controls. “Moderate” means the architecture should cope if Chapter 18 controls operate. “High” means failure of one control can cause material harm. “Critical” means the scenario can defeat several safeguards or expose unresolved authority, property, public finance or remedy. Uncertainty is preserved, not hidden in a confidence score.

Pakistan’s starting point is neither prohibition nor a completed market. The VAA is operative and already supplies functional scope, licensing, customer-asset, issuer, AML/CFT, enforcement and delegated-law architecture. But the official record reviewed at the cut-off still describes the comprehensive VASP Regulations as draft, the NOC stage as current and full licensing as forthcoming.436 That starting condition matters: a future scenario cannot be tested honestly by assuming that every Chapter 18 correction has already been enacted or implemented.

International materials confirm that implementation variability is itself a future driver. The FSB’s 2025 thematic review records progress but significant gaps and inconsistencies, particularly for global stablecoin arrangements and cross-border coordination.437 FATF’s 2025 update likewise identifies continuing difficulty with offshore VASPs, persons exercising control in DeFi, stablecoins, fraud, recovery and Travel Rule implementation.438 These findings do not forecast Pakistan’s market. They justify testing a domestic regime against cross-border activity, functional ambiguity and uneven foreign cooperation.
