The matrix is deliberately divergent. A completed licensing framework may coexist with a stablecoin run. Tokenisation may grow while unbacked trading contracts. Cross-border rules may harmonise in one function and fragment in another. The useful result is not a single narrative. It is a set of conditions under which a regulator, court, ministry or legislature knows what evidence to watch and what decision it must be prepared to make.

19.2 Baseline order: prolonged incompleteness

Assumption. The VAA remains operative, NOC and transition cases continue to require administration, final regulatory modules or connected instruments arrive unevenly, and a material share of customer activity remains offshore or outside a clearly evidenced domestic permission. This is a continuation scenario, not a claim that delay will occur.

The legal stress is produced by time. An NOC, pending application, sandbox permission, saved Ordinance-era instrument and statutory licence are different legal states. If the public register, completeness method, transition determination, appointment record and review route remain incomplete, repeated administrative practice may harden into market expectation without acquiring legal authority. Banks, customers and foreign counterparties may then rely on inconsistent descriptions of who is permitted to do what.

The affected interests are broader than applicants. Customers may believe that regulatory engagement equals full supervision. Compliant firms may bear higher costs than offshore competitors. Banks may either over-exclude legitimate applicants or supply access without a complete regulatory status. PVARA staff may be asked to decide under criteria not yet contained in valid instruments. A court may receive an urgent dispute before the Tribunal, record-transfer process or digital-asset custody mechanism is demonstrably operational.

Current law is not empty during this scenario. Direct statutory duties concerning unauthorised activity, customer assets, conduct, AML/CFT, cooperation and enforcement remain relevant according to their terms.439 The danger is selective operability: coercive powers may be invoked before corresponding procedures, reasons and remedies work; businesses may face duties without a usable application path; or customers may receive warnings without a practical return or complaint route.

The no-regret response is therefore Chapter 18’s Horizon I package: publish exact status; authenticate appointments and delegations; maintain the authoritative instruments register; verify the lawful review and investigation routes; decide section 74 continuity instrument by instrument; and state which requirements apply during transition. Government should progress only those measures for which authority and implementation capacity are proved. It should not compensate for delay by presenting a draft handbook as binding or by announcing scale targets.

Early indicators. The dashboard should watch the age and legal status of NOC and licence applications; number of publicly unclassified providers; frequency of banks requesting regulator confirmation; customer complaints caused by status confusion; unpublished or superseded documents still used in decisions; vacancies and unverified delegations; inability to file an appeal; and the proportion of supervisory actions later withdrawn for procedural reasons.

Residual risk and implication. Even a candid transition notice cannot eliminate litigation over accrued positions or the exact operation of section 70. The design implication is to preserve customer continuity while refusing legal fiction. If the baseline persists, the response is targeted amendment or a lawfully made instrument—not indefinite administrative tolerance. Uncertainty: neither the duration of incomplete implementation nor the scale of offshore substitution can be responsibly quantified from the verified record.

19.3 Regulated-market deepening

Assumption. The amendment, Rules and final Regulations contemplated by Chapter 18 are substantially completed; PVARA grants activity-specific permissions; banks supply controlled account access; and supervised domestic providers begin to mediate a greater range of customer activity. This scenario tests success conditions rather than assuming that authorisation itself is success.

The first stress is supervisory load. A licence converts a prospective assessment into a continuing obligation to supervise ownership, governance, capital, custody, conduct, AML/CFT, technology, outsourcing and wind-down. If licence issuance outpaces trained staff, reliable returns and inspection capability, the system may create a stronger appearance of safety than the evidence warrants. The risk increases if a small number of exchanges, custodians, banks, cloud providers or analytics vendors become essential across the market.

The second stress is multi-function concentration. An exchange may combine brokerage, custody, lending, proprietary dealing, token listing, settlement, staking and issuance support. Legal-entity approval cannot erase conflicts between these functions. Customer assets may support settlement exposure; proprietary trading may influence listing or execution; and group entities may shift risk beyond the licensed perimeter. The FSB and IOSCO frameworks both treat functional coverage, conflicts, data and cross-border cooperation as necessary parts of implementation rather than consequences that follow automatically from licensing.440

The third stress is connected-law dependency. A PVARA permission cannot supply SBP payment or foreign-exchange authority, SECP securities authority, FBR tax treatment, provincial services-tax treatment, property title or an environmental approval. Market deepening therefore tests the joint perimeter and referral mechanism more severely than a small transitional market. A delayed decision by one institution can block a lawful product; an informal concurrence can expose all institutions to challenge.

Chapter 18 remains resilient if licences carry a machine- and human-readable permission schedule; every provider has a named supervisory owner; capital and customer assets are independently reconciled; material outsourcing and group exposure are mapped; cross-regulator determinations are published; and an exercised wind-down route exists. Expansion should be sequenced by risk, with custody, exchange, lending, leverage, payment and issuer permissions subject to stronger evidence than low-footprint advice.

The market should not be measured by licence count alone. Early indicators include assets and customers per provider; share of custody, liquidity, cloud and banking dependencies concentrated in the largest entities; capital exceptions; reconciliation breaks; complaints per activity; unresolved perimeter referrals; frequency and age of prudential remediation; staff-to-risk ratios; and the proportion of providers capable of completing an exit exercise. A rapid increase in licensed volume combined with flat supervisory coverage is an escalation trigger, not a success indicator.

Residual risk and implication. Regulation can shift risk rather than remove it: into concentrated providers, shared infrastructure, group entities or customer belief in State guarantee. The legal design should therefore preserve resolution, portability and failure planning from the first licence. Uncertainty: the verified record does not establish the future number, scale, ownership or business model of licensed providers, or the degree to which Pakistani customers will move from offshore channels.

19.4 Stablecoin and payment stress

Assumption. One or more fiat- or asset-referenced tokens become materially used by Pakistani customers for conversion, remittance, merchant settlement, savings-like balances, DeFi collateral or cross-border trade. The scenario does not assume that such use is lawful in every form, that a token is legal tender, or that adoption reaches any numerical threshold.

Stablecoin scale compresses several legal events into a fast technical path: acquisition with rupees or foreign currency; custody or self-hosting; cross-border transfer; conversion; payment instruction; merchant settlement; reserve redemption; and accounting or tax recognition. Different institutions may own each decision. The VAA provides fiat- and asset-referenced categories and issuer/reserve architecture, but SBP retains currency, banking, payment and foreign-exchange authority under its laws. Contractual acceptance by a merchant does not convert the token into legal tender or settle the legality of the conversion and payment legs.

Three failure mechanisms should be tested. First, an issuer run may arise from doubt about reserve quality, custody, legal title, redemption, banking access or sanctions. Secondly, a gateway interruption may prevent conversion or merchant settlement even where the token continues to trade on-chain. Thirdly, a cross-border integrity shock may cause foreign issuers, banks or platforms to freeze addresses or restrict a jurisdiction, leaving customers with an asset they cannot lawfully or practically redeem.

The financial-integrity stress is substantial. FATF’s 2025 update reports increasing illicit use of stablecoins, continuing offshore-VASP challenges and weak recovery after major thefts; its revised Recommendation 16 also changes international payment-transparency expectations.441 These are global observations, not findings about Pakistani users. They justify a system capable of identifying originator, beneficiary, provider, self-hosted address risk and lawful freeze or rejection without treating every stablecoin transfer as illicit.

The monetary and prudential stress is different. BIS’s 2026 analysis recognises tokenisation’s potential while concluding that current stablecoin arrangements do not supply all foundational properties of money and may create integrity and macro-financial challenges at scale.442 For Pakistan, the relevant question is not whether a foreign report prefers another monetary architecture. It is whether reserve, redemption, liquidity, currency substitution, FX, settlement and loss allocation can be governed under Pakistani law.

Chapter 18’s FRT module should therefore be tested before material retail or payment scale. The test requires a legally identified issuer; holder claim; reserve ownership, custody, composition and valuation; daily or risk-based reconciliation; redemption time and suspension grounds; payment and FX permissions; customer-money treatment; settlement finality; refunds and chargebacks; AML/Travel Rule interoperability; insolvency; and a coordinated run plan. A reserve attestation without liability, control and redemption evidence is insufficient.

Early indicators. Authorities should monitor, under lawful data powers, stablecoin exposure by provider and use rather than publicity estimates; concentration by issuer, reserve custodian and blockchain; redemption requests and delay; deviations from the promised reference; changes in issuer terms; bank or gateway interruptions; use as DeFi collateral; self-hosted and cross-border transfer patterns; sanctions or freezing events; customer complaints about convertibility; and differences between on-chain supply evidence and provider liabilities.

Residual risk and implication. Pakistan cannot compel a foreign issuer, reserve bank or blockchain to continue service. Domestic rules can limit exposure, require local accountability, preserve evidence and create an exit route, but cannot guarantee parity. The legal design implication is to cap or condition retail, payment or public-sector reliance until redemption and failure tests pass, and to require SBP–PVARA–FMU coordination before crisis. Uncertainty: future stablecoin use, reserve location, issuer cooperation and the speed of a confidence shock are unknown; no adoption or loss figure is forecast.

19.5 Tokenised assets and capital-market expansion

Assumption. Regulated firms or public bodies pilot or offer tokenised shares, debt, fund interests, commodities, warehouse goods, land-related claims or other real-world assets. Demand may come from domestic investors, diaspora, institutions or cross-border platforms, but the scenario assigns no volume or success probability.

Tokenisation can reduce reconciliation friction and make transfer conditions programmable, but it also creates a second representation of a legal right. The central stress is divergence: the token ledger shows one holder while the company register, depository, land record, warehouse document, secured-transactions registry or custodian record shows another. A technically final transfer may be legally ineffective; a valid court order may not propagate on-chain; or an oracle may report that an off-chain condition occurred when it did not.

The applicable law follows the underlying right and function. A token representing a share or investment may engage securities, company, depository and market-infrastructure law. A token purporting to represent land or goods depends on the law governing title, registration, possession and priority. The VAA can govern issuance services, virtual-asset conduct and custody, but it does not make every tokenised claim valid or displace SECP, registrar, provincial or judicial authority.443

The stress chain should test six events: valid initial creation; disclosure and investor classification; transfer and settlement; corporate action or income distribution; creation and enforcement of a security interest; and issuer, custodian or platform insolvency. It should also test a lost key, erroneous transfer, fork, frozen wallet, fraudulent duplicate token and mismatch between token supply and legally outstanding rights.

Chapter 18’s issuer and RWA bridge remains adequate only if every project has a legal-rights memorandum and an authoritative-record design. The memorandum should identify issuer and obligor, holder’s enforceable claim, governing law, authoritative register, transfer formalities, restrictions, custody, perfection, priority, corporate actions, tax, enforcement and insolvency. The system should specify when the token ledger is authoritative, evidential or merely operational, and who can lawfully correct divergence.

International work supplies evidence of possibilities and preconditions, not Pakistani authority. BIS work on tokenisation identifies potential use in payments and financial transactions and emphasises the legal, governance and operational foundations needed for deployment.444 The correct domestic pilot therefore links technical tests to a recognised asset and institutional owner. A sandbox decision cannot validate title, waive public procurement, or substitute for a securities approval.

Early indicators. The dashboard should record asset classes proposed; classification time; percentage of pilots with complete legal-rights memoranda; authoritative-register integration; reconciliation exceptions; corporate actions requiring manual correction; rejected or reversed transfers; custody concentration; secondary-market liquidity; investor complaints; and unresolved questions of perfection, tax or jurisdiction. A project should stop if the underlying registry cannot recognise or correct the tokenised state.

Residual risk and implication. Some legal rights may not be suitable for tokenisation without primary amendment or registry reform. Parallel records can increase, rather than reduce, operational complexity. The design implication is “registry before token”: identify the legal source of truth and correction authority before public issuance. Uncertainty: it is unknown which asset classes will present a lawful cost advantage over existing electronic systems, and no efficiency or capital-raising outcome is assumed.

19.6 DeFi, DAO and autonomous-agent diffusion

Assumption. Pakistani customers obtain material access to decentralised exchanges, lending pools, staking arrangements, DAO-governed services or AI systems that recommend, initiate or manage virtual-asset transactions. Access may occur through local interfaces, foreign applications, wallets, APIs or general-purpose agents. The scenario does not assume that a protocol is decentralised merely because its code is public or its governance uses tokens.

The first stress is factual attribution. A protocol may involve developers, deployers, interface operators, governance participants, oracle providers, administrators, multisignature signers, liquidity suppliers, fee recipients and users. Their legal significance differs. IOSCO’s DeFi work treats claims of decentralisation as facts to be examined through control, influence, economic interest and operational roles, while preserving the need to apply the relevant legal framework.445 Pakistan should use those indicators to investigate, not to impose automatic developer or token-holder liability.

The second stress is authority. An automated system may form or perform a contract, route an order, rebalance assets, vote, borrow, liquidate collateral or transmit a payment. Pakistan’s Electronic Transactions Ordinance supports electronic form and attribution of automated communications to a person using or controlling the system, but attribution does not resolve consent, authority, mistake, fiduciary obligation, market conduct or remedy. The VAA’s functional definitions and control concepts may reach a service or issuer without conferring personality on code.446

An AI agent sharpens this problem because it may select tools and actions not individually specified by the user. A provider could describe the output as information while the system actually personalises advice, exercises discretion or executes transactions. A customer may give a broad natural-language instruction that the agent converts into a chain of swaps, approvals and protocol interactions. The legal analysis must separate the user’s mandate, deployer’s design, model provider, wallet permission, interface, execution venue and any human override.

The third stress is common-mode behaviour. If many firms use the same model, data source, cloud service, oracle or agent framework, apparently independent decisions may become correlated. The FSB identifies third-party concentration, market correlation, cyber risk, model risk, data quality and governance as potential financial-system vulnerabilities from AI adoption.447 In digital-asset markets, those vulnerabilities can combine with continuous trading, automated liquidation and thin liquidity.

Chapter 18’s functional perimeter remains resilient if final rules require an automated-system responsibility file. It should identify the legally accountable deployer; permitted task; customer mandate; activity classification; data and model dependencies; wallet and API permissions; transaction and value limits; testing; monitoring; override and shutdown; record of prompts, policy and actions where lawful; incident response; customer explanation; and remedy. The file should be proportionate, protect trade secrets and personal data, and preserve sufficient evidence to contest a decision.

DeFi regulation should focus on the accessible service and actual control. A local interface that selects assets, routes trades, controls fees or can suspend access may carry responsibilities even if it cannot alter the base protocol. An immutable protocol may still depend on an oracle, stablecoin, bridge, hosting layer or governance process. Conversely, writing code, holding a token or casting one vote should not be treated as conclusive proof of regulated control, partnership, agency or breach.

NIST’s 2026 concept paper on software and AI-agent identity and authorisation is expressly a draft project concept, not a legal standard, but it identifies a concrete design issue: autonomous systems need distinguishable identities and bounded access to data, tools and applications.448 Pakistan should test agent credentials, least privilege, separation of customer accounts, revocation, transaction signing, human confirmation for defined actions and attribution logs before an agent receives custody or execution authority.

Early indicators. Relevant signals include material customer losses involving automated execution; growth in agent-controlled wallet permissions; common model, oracle, bridge or cloud dependencies; repeated overrides; actions outside mandate; unexplained correlated trading; prompt-injection or data-poisoning events; DAO administrator-key use; governance concentration; interface delisting or shutdown; and inability to reconstruct why and by whose authority a transaction occurred.

Residual risk and implication. Adaptive output cannot always be predicted or explained at transaction-level precision, and a foreign protocol may lack a reachable operator. The design implication is not a fictional electronic person. It is bounded authority, attributable deployment, observable control, intervention capacity, records and loss allocation. High-impact autonomous custody, execution or payment should remain restricted until those elements pass testing. Uncertainty: the capabilities, deployment patterns and genuine autonomy of future agents and protocols are unknown.

19.7 Cyber, fraud or institutional-failure shock

Assumption. A material event affects one or more critical providers or public institutions: compromise of signing keys; insider theft; corrupted entitlement data; cloud or telecommunications outage; bridge or oracle exploit; ransomware; coordinated fraud; reserve freeze; or absence of a lawfully authorised decision-maker during the event. The scenario is compound because digital-asset failures rarely respect institutional boundaries.

The first minutes produce an authority problem. Who can halt withdrawals, isolate a wallet, direct preservation, notify customers, obtain a court order, contact a foreign provider or decide that continued operation is unsafe? A technically capable person without lawful power may protect assets but contaminate evidence or infringe rights; a legally authorised official without keys, data or a working communication channel may be unable to act. Chapter 15’s authentication and responsibility protocol is therefore part of cyber resilience, not separate governance work.

The next phase produces a property and evidence problem. The provider must distinguish customer and house assets, valid and fraudulent instructions, on-chain and off-chain liabilities, frozen and lost assets, and recoverable and irrecoverable keys. Investigators need a preserved chain connecting system logs, wallet control, transaction data, device evidence and human decisions. Customers need accurate notice and access to funds that are not lawfully restricted. A premature public attribution can trigger withdrawals or prejudice proceedings; silence can deepen harm.

Fraud may exploit the same event. FATF’s 2025 update describes increasing fraud and scam exposure, major theft, stablecoin misuse and low recovery in a significant cross-border case.449 These global findings do not measure Pakistan. They demonstrate why the plan must cover impersonation, false recovery services, compromised customer communications, mule accounts, dormant accounts and rapid layering after the original breach.

The Chapter 18 package supplies four linked safeguards. First, the customer-asset and failure plan allows reconstruction and transfer. Secondly, the incident standard supplies severity, contacts, update duties and recovery evidence. Thirdly, the investigation SOP supplies preservation, key custody, legal process and return. Fourthly, the Tribunal and court route supplies interim relief and challenge. None is sufficient alone. A technically successful freeze without review can become unlawful deprivation; a perfect evidential chain without customer-asset records may prove the loss but not restore the asset.

The exercise should run without advance notice to the operational team while protecting live systems. It should simulate unavailable senior officers, a conflicted service provider, cross-border data, a disputed customer claim and an incorrect initial indicator. The after-action record should distinguish decision, authority, evidence, elapsed time, customer impact, failed dependency and remediation. Security-sensitive details can be protected, but the public should receive an accountable summary.

The heat map is a consequence comparison, not a probability map. Its central result is that the compound shock can defeat all modules simultaneously, while otherwise distinct scenarios repeatedly stress coordination and remedy. The common corrective priority is therefore a tested decision chain, not another general statement that cyber risk is important.

Early indicators. Signals include privileged-access anomalies; key-policy exceptions; unresolved reconciliation breaks; vendor or cloud concentration; repeated high-severity vulnerabilities; fraudulent domain and social-media impersonation; abrupt withdrawal or complaint spikes; delayed incident classification; inconsistent public statements; unavailable decision-makers; evidence-transfer failures; and orders that cannot be implemented by custodians or foreign platforms.

Residual risk and implication. No architecture prevents every theft, outage or fraud. Foreign recovery may fail, technical intervention may be unavailable, and compensation may not cover loss. The design implication is to minimise irreversible exposure, preserve lawful options and practise failure. Uncertainty: the initiating event, target, duration, asset-recovery rate and contagion path cannot be predicted and are not assigned probabilities.

19.8 Cross-border fragmentation or harmonisation

Assumption. Foreign jurisdictions continue to implement crypto-asset, stablecoin, tax, payment, sanctions, data and AI rules at different speeds. Some requirements converge through international standards while market-access, custody, issuer, privacy and enforcement rules remain incompatible. Pakistan may face both demands for recognition and restrictions by foreign providers.

The scenario stresses section 4 extraterritorial reach and sections 9 and 17 cooperation and recognition powers. An offshore platform may target Pakistan without a conventional establishment; a foreign issuer may serve local wallets but deny local jurisdiction; or a Pakistan licensee may depend on a custodian whose home regulator restricts service. Two authorities may demand inconsistent retention, disclosure, freezing or customer treatment. A memorandum can facilitate exchange but cannot create coercive power or extinguish a Pakistani remedy.

The FSB’s 2025 review identifies gaps and inconsistencies in implementation and the resulting opportunity for regulatory arbitrage.450 FATF’s revised Recommendation 16 increases convergence around payment-message information, but international convergence does not itself decide Pakistan’s domestic authority, privacy safeguards or technical interface.451 Tax reporting adds another lane: CARF-style exchange requires domestic fiscal authority, due diligence, secure systems and an international legal basis, not a PVARA licence alone.

Chapter 18’s issue-specific recognition model is robust if every reliance decision identifies the activity, comparable outcome, home supervisor, data and record access, customer-asset location, local service and complaint route, enforcement cooperation, transition and withdrawal. Recognition should reduce duplicate evidence only where cooperation works. Material retail, custody, payment or stablecoin exposure may require local conditions even when a foreign licence is respected for a limited function.

The contrary path—fragmentation—requires an exit playbook. PVARA should be able to identify affected customers, assets, dependencies and contractual rights; require notice and transfer; preserve records; coordinate with SBP, FMU, tax and enforcement bodies; and state what Pakistan can and cannot compel. An untested promise of international cooperation is not a safeguard.

Early indicators. The dashboard should track foreign legal changes affecting Pakistan access; rejected supervisory requests; delayed or incomplete Travel Rule messages; foreign licence restrictions; concentration in jurisdictions without effective cooperation; conflicts over data, sanctions or freezes; sudden terms-of-service changes; blocked redemptions or withdrawals; and growing targeted solicitation by unregistered offshore providers.

Residual risk and implication. Pakistan cannot harmonise foreign law unilaterally and should not trade away constitutional, monetary, tax or customer-protection requirements for nominal access. The design implication is selective interoperability with an executable withdrawal route. Uncertainty: foreign reforms, equivalence decisions, geopolitical conditions and provider cooperation are external variables; neither harmonisation nor fragmentation is presumed dominant.

19.9 Mining, energy and environmental pathway

Assumption. Public or private actors seek to expand virtual-asset mining because of claimed surplus generation, changing tariffs, investment proposals or new equipment economics—or existing operations contract or migrate when those conditions change. PVARA may regulate a mining-related virtual-asset service, but it does not allocate power, approve a connection, set a tariff or grant environmental permission.

The main stress is temporal mismatch. Electricity described as surplus at one hour, season or network location may have another use at a different time. A long-lived concession based on a short-lived surplus can shift grid, fuel, capacity, transmission or environmental cost to households, firms or public finance. Technology may also change the revenue per unit of energy before the State recovers infrastructure or fiscal cost.

International evidence establishes the materiality of energy and emissions, not Pakistan’s local balance. IMF analysis links crypto mining and data centres to growing electricity demand and environmental externalities and cautions against special fiscal treatment without accounting for grid and social cost.452 Its global estimates and proposed tax rates are not transplanted into Pakistani law or treated as local measurements.

Chapter 18’s approval stack should govern every project: verified load and location; generation and transmission evidence; lawful connection and tariff; curtailment priority; metering; environmental screening and approval; water and equipment-disposal effects where material; land and local permission; tax and customs treatment; procurement or allocation authority; public-money control; employment and technology claims; and termination if the factual premise changes. Provincial and federal institutions must act within their own laws.

Early indicators. Relevant signals are requested and connected load; hourly and seasonal utilisation; curtailment and grid congestion; tariff recovery and arrears; fuel and foreign-exchange exposure; emissions and environmental non-compliance; water or equipment-waste impacts; fiscal incentives; public infrastructure cost; jobs and local expenditure actually delivered; unauthorised mining; and divergence between projected and verified revenue.

Residual risk and implication. Even a compliant project may become uneconomic or impose opportunity costs when energy conditions change. The design implication is a reversible, measured permission—not a strategic entitlement. Uncertainty: future mining technology, asset economics, energy mix, location and genuinely available surplus are unknown; no public return is forecast.

19.10 Rights and distribution under the scenarios

None of the scenarios is distributionally neutral. The same control can protect one interest and burden another. Enhanced traceability may reduce fraud but expose financial associations; a rapid freeze may preserve assets but restrict innocent property; high capital requirements may protect customers but concentrate the market; local-presence rules may improve remedy but exclude a useful foreign service; and mining revenue may benefit one region while electricity or environmental cost falls elsewhere.

The constitutional frame remains legality, fair treatment, privacy and dignity, economic freedom subject to law, property, equality, information, federal distribution of authority and effective judicial review. These rights do not decide every policy outcome, but they require lawful source, rational classification, proportionality where rights are restricted, reasons and remedy.453

Table 19.1 — Cross-scenario rights and distribution test

Interest/groupBenefit that may ariseConcentrated riskRequired safeguard and proof
Retail customersLawful access, competition and faster serviceLoss, misleading status, illiquidity and weak remedyPermission disclosure, asset protection, complaints and tested return
Remittance users and diasporaLower-friction transfer or programmable settlementFX breach, depeg, gateway failure and data exposureSBP/PVARA allocation, redemption, price/fee disclosure and alternate route
Small firms and innovatorsModular entry and shared infrastructureFixed-cost exclusion and dependence on dominant providersProportionate requirements, sandbox limits, open standards and competition monitoring
Persons subject to monitoringFraud protection and correction of misdirected transfersExcess collection, false match, opaque analytics and onward disclosurePurpose, minimisation, access control, correction, audit and lawful challenge
Customers whose assets are frozenPreservation and possible recoveryIndefinite or mistaken deprivationThreshold, record, notice where lawful, time limit, review and return

The rights test must occur at design and incident stages. A lawful data field can become disproportionate when retained indefinitely or shared for a new purpose. An emergency restriction can become unlawful when urgency ends. An algorithmic risk score can support triage but should not become an undisclosed reason for licence refusal, account closure or enforcement. Human review must have authority and enough information to change the result.

Distribution should also be measured by who can exit. A sophisticated institution may diversify custodians, verify reserves and litigate abroad; a retail user may rely on a phone interface and regulatory badge. Chapter 18’s portability, reasons and remedy controls therefore protect capability, not merely formal equality. The National Digital Masterplan framework can coordinate inclusion and infrastructure, but it cannot authorise sector regulation or override rights.454

Cross-scenario implication. The dashboard should disaggregate complaints, losses, freezes, service interruptions, licensing outcomes and remediation where lawful and statistically responsible. It should test whether burdens cluster by customer type, region, gender, disability, business size or access channel without turning protected data into a new risk. Uncertainty: distributional effects depend on actual use and institutional behaviour; no inclusion or employment benefit is presumed.

19.11 Decision triggers, early indicators and no-regret moves

Anticipatory intelligence becomes useful only when an indicator is connected to a lawful decision. A dashboard that reports rising stablecoin use but does not identify who can act, under what provision, with what evidence and remedy is market commentary, not governance. The Chapter 18 implementation register should therefore add a scenario field to each corrective item: which future condition it protects against, what signal activates review and what response is available before primary law changes.

For this dashboard, three operational levels are proposed. Watch means an indicator changed and its lead must verify source and context. Escalate means an adopted threshold or qualitative condition has been met and responsible institutions must assess exposure and options. Act means the legal condition for a defined intervention has been proved. A trigger never invents power. Where authority is absent, the response is amendment, court process, referral to the competent institution or limitation of a voluntary programme.

The threshold for an indicator should be adopted by the institution with legal and technical competence. Some can be numerical—capital, reconciliation tolerance or outage impact—once evidence exists. Others are necessarily qualitative: loss of a lawful decision-maker, inability to identify the holder’s claim, or conflict between two binding commands. The dashboard should show source, data quality, version and the reason an alert was opened or closed.

No-regret moves

Eight measures improve resilience across every scenario without presuming which one occurs:

1. maintain a public, versioned register of legal instruments, permissions, decisions and institutional authority;

2. make the PVARA–SBP–SECP–FMU perimeter and incident routes operational through test cases;

3. require reconstructable customer assets, liabilities, keys and dependencies, with an exercised return plan;

4. establish interoperable AML/Travel Rule and sanctions processes with privacy, correction and protected access;

5. authenticate the Tribunal, investigation and urgent-review routes before coercive crisis action;

6. record concentration in providers, banks, custodians, cloud, analytics, bridges, oracles and AI models;

7. run compound exercises that include legal, customer, communication, evidence and cross-border failure; and

8. publish outcome evidence and residual risk so that scale, restriction or legislative correction is reasoned.

These moves implement rather than enlarge Chapter 18. Their legal basis must still be identified item by item.455 They should be reviewed quarterly at programme level, immediately after a material event and independently after the first full operational cycle. The review should preserve false alarms and rejected evidence; otherwise the State cannot learn whether its indicators are useful.

Handoff to Chapter 20 — machine-executable regulation

Chapter 20 should express the dashboard in machine-consumable form without allowing code to decide legal authority. Each indicator requires: stable identifier; source; status; effective version; data owner; condition; evidence or data-quality limitation—not scenario probability; accountable institution; lawful actions; mandatory consultation; safeguard; evidence; reasons; remedy; expiry and review. `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states must block a system from presenting a proposed or absent rule as operative.

Agent identity and authorisation are suitable technical tests; statutory interpretation, proportionality, contested facts, institutional competence and remedy remain human legal judgments. International AI frameworks can inform governance, mapping, measurement and deactivation, but they do not allocate Pakistani power.456 The machine-readable result should therefore generate a traceable alert and decision file, not an automatic freeze, licence refusal, tax charge or finding of liability.

The chapter’s conclusion is conditional but firm. Pakistan does not need to know which scenario will occur in order to make authority visible, protect customer assets, connect regulators, preserve evidence, test remedies and watch concentration. Those are no-regret foundations. The future question is not whether code, stablecoins, tokenisation or AI will inevitably transform finance. It is whether the legal order can recognise a material change early, identify the competent decision-maker, act within law, distribute loss fairly and revise itself on evidence.

-## 19.2 Law as Code, Rules as Code and the authority boundary
-“Law as Code” and “Rules as Code” are useful only if their meanings are separated. **Law as Code** is the broader inquiry into how legal norms can be represented, tested or implemented computationally and how code itself structures conduct. **Rules as Code** is a public-administration method: selected rules are expressed in machine-consumable form, ideally through a multidisciplinary process conn
-Four artefacts may coexist:
-| Artefact | What it does | What it cannot prove |
-|---|---|---|
-| authenticated human-readable instrument | states the enacted or validly made rule in its authoritative form | that an administrative or software implementation is correct |
-| structured legal representation | identifies provisions, definitions, amendments, relationships and metadata | that every provision is reducible to determinate logic |
-| executable model | applies declared conditions, calculations or routes to supplied inputs | legal truth of contested inputs, institutional competence or lawful exercise of discretion |
-| service implementation | collects evidence, calls the model, records action and communicates with a user | authority beyond the governing law or immunity from reasons, review and remedy |
-The OECD’s 2020 working paper describes Rules as Code as an official machine-consumable version produced alongside human-readable rules and treats it as a change in rulemaking, not merely a software project. It also records limitations and competing conceptions rather than presenting one mature global standard.[^446] New Zealand’s Better Rules discovery similarly used multidisciplinary teams and
-The distinction between **machine-readable**, **machine-consumable** and **machine-executable** should be maintained. A provision with a stable identifier, dates and subject tags is machine-readable. A structured obligation that a service can query is machine-consumable. A rule that evaluates inputs and returns a result is executable. Each transition adds interpretation and therefore adds a new p
-The terms describe capability, not authority.
-Standardised identifiers and metadata can improve access without purporting to decide cases. The European Legislation Identifier, for example, uses persistent identifiers and structured metadata so legislation can be accessed, exchanged and reused across systems.[^448] Pakistan can learn from that publication architecture without importing European law or assuming that linked data resolves statut
-Three propositions follow.
-First, official status is a legal question. A government-hosted file may be a consultation draft, guidance, a consolidated convenience copy or an operative instrument. A machine must carry that status, not infer authority from a domain name. Secondly, equivalence between text and model cannot be self-declared by the developer. It requires legal mapping, test cases and approval within the relevant
-This report therefore uses a deliberately bounded formulation: Qānūn-Map may make legal requirements more **legible, traceable and testable**. It does not make public power self-executing. “Code is law” is rejected both descriptively and constitutionally. Code can constrain a workflow, but only law can supply the State’s authority to burden a person, and only an authorised process can turn proved
-## 19.3 Qānūn-Map: a human-governed legal knowledge architecture
-Qānūn-Map is the proposed name for a linked legal knowledge and decision-support architecture. It is not a new legal order and, at the present stage, is not a deployed public system. Its purpose is to preserve the path from source to implementation in a form usable by lawyers, drafters, regulators, service designers, engineers, regulated persons and reviewers.
-The architecture contains seven connected stores or services:
-1. an **authoritative-source register** containing instruments, issuers, official locations, authentication evidence, dates, status and checksums;
-2. a **norm map** that divides instruments into addressable provisions and records definitions, powers, duties, exceptions, amendments, dependencies and conflicts;
-3. an **obligation model** expressing the actor, activity, condition, duty, exception, evidence, institution, decision, reason and remedy;
-4. an **evidence schema** defining what a supplied fact means, its source, custodian, quality, time and permissible use;
-5. a **test suite** containing ordinary cases, boundary cases, missing-input cases, conflicts, amendments and prohibited outcomes;
-6. a **decision-file service** that records the model and source version used, questions asked, inputs supplied, path, warnings, human officer, reasons and action; and
-7. a **review and change layer** for correction, appeal, legal update, regression testing, rollback, publication and audit.
-**Figure 19.1 — From legal text to a reviewable Qānūn-Map**
+# Chapter 19 — Future: Scenarios and Anticipatory Legal Intelligence
+> **Status and evidence cut-off.** Substantive working draft for Author review. Legal and institutional status is checked to 16 August 2026. The scenarios are conditional tests, not forecasts, probabilities, price projections or claims that any technology, market structure or reform will occur.
+## 19.1 Scenario method, horizon and uncertainty
+The purpose of foresight in this report is not to predict which token will succeed, how many Pakistanis will use a wallet, or when a global market cycle will turn. Its purpose is to expose decisions that become dangerous if they are first considered during a run, a failure, a constitutional challenge or a rapid shift in market structure. Chapter 18 supplied the corrective package. Chapter 19 asks
+The scenarios use two planning horizons measured from a formally adopted implementation start. The **operational horizon** covers the period in which legal instruments, licensing, interfaces, supervisory systems and remedies are being made functional. The **structural horizon** covers the later period in which scale, concentration, new technical forms or changed international standards may test t
+Each scenario is constructed from seven elements:
+1. an explicit assumption about market, technology or institutional conditions;
+2. the law, institution or operational dependency placed under stress;
+3. the mechanism by which the system could fail or produce unequal loss;
+4. the persons, rights, assets and public interests affected;
+5. safeguards already present in law or proposed in Chapter 18;
+6. the residual risk after those safeguards; and
+7. an observable indicator that should trigger review before the failure becomes acute.
+The stress ratings used below describe **consequence if the scenario occurs**, not likelihood. “Low” means the stress is secondary and contained by ordinary controls. “Moderate” means the architecture should cope if Chapter 18 controls operate. “High” means failure of one control can cause material harm. “Critical” means the scenario can defeat several safeguards or expose unresolved authority, p
+Pakistan’s starting point is neither prohibition nor a completed market. The VAA is operative and already supplies functional scope, licensing, customer-asset, issuer, AML/CFT, enforcement and delegated-law architecture. But the official record reviewed at the cut-off still describes the comprehensive VASP Regulations as draft, the NOC stage as current and full licensing as forthcoming.[^436] Tha
+International materials confirm that implementation variability is itself a future driver. The FSB’s 2025 thematic review records progress but significant gaps and inconsistencies, particularly for global stablecoin arrangements and cross-border coordination.[^437] FATF’s 2025 update likewise identifies continuing difficulty with offshore VASPs, persons exercising control in DeFi, stablecoins, fr

Internal convenience must not become an undisclosed condition of eligibility

-## 19.4 Normative hierarchy, source status and version control
-Qānūn-Map should encode authority before it encodes outcomes. That authority cannot be represented as one universal ladder in which every source simply ranks above or below every other. It must preserve several legal dimensions:
-| Authority dimension | Rule for the model |
-|---|---|
-| constitutional supremacy | no statute, delegated instrument or administrative act may be treated as valid authority contrary to the Constitution as lawfully interpreted |
-| legislative competence | identify whether the matter and instrument are federal or provincial and apply the constitutional distribution and conflict rules; do not assume that one legislature’s Act universally ranks above the other’s |
-| delegated legislation | link each Rule, Regulation, notification or other instrument to its enabling Act, maker, procedure, Gazette status, scope and consistency limits; instrument names alone do not establish an inter se rank |
-| judicial authority | record court, bench, date, precedential status, issue and material factual setting; precedent operates through the judicial hierarchy and legal doctrine, not as another paragraph in a legislative stack |
-| administrative act | identify the statutory power, delegate, case, reasons and review status; an administrative decision may determine a case within power but is not equivalent to general legislation |
-| guidance and operations | label standards, circulars, forms, FAQs and internal instructions by their actual legal effect; publication in software does not promote them into binding law |
-The Virtual Assets Act illustrates why this matters. The Act came into force at once and authorises federal Rules by Gazette notification and PVARA Regulations through the statutory procedure. Its direct provisions coexist with matters left to prescription. The official material checked for this report continued to distinguish the Act, NOC stage, draft VASP Regulations and prospective full licens
-Every source object should contain at least:
-| Field | Required content |
-|---|---|
-| identity | jurisdiction, instrument type, official title, number and stable provision ID |
-| authority | issuing body, enabling provision and authentication evidence |
-| status | `OPERATIVE_VERIFIED`, `[DRAFT]`, `[GAP]`, `HISTORICAL`, `SUPERSEDED`, `SUSPENDED` or `NOT_READ` |
-| time | making, publication, commencement, effective-from, effective-to and transition dates |
-| text | exact provision, language, official locator and any authorised correction |
-| relationship | amends, repeals, saves, overrides, depends on, conflicts with or implements |
-| integrity | file checksum, extraction method, reviewer and last verified date |
-| model link | rule objects, test suite, implementation version and release approval |
-The system should distinguish **source version**, **model version**, **engine version** and **service version**. A statute can remain unchanged while a faulty model is corrected. A model can remain unchanged while the evaluation engine changes. A service interface can change without altering either. Combining all four under “latest version” makes audit impossible.
-Updates must never be silent. A source change enters quarantine; a legal owner verifies authority and temporal effect; the model is amended in a separate branch; the full test suite runs; affected institutions approve within their functions; and a signed release states which cases may change. If urgent legal change precedes a tested model, the safe response is to suspend the affected automated ro
-Temporal logic deserves separate testing. Publication, commencement, transition, savings, repeal and retrospective effect are not interchangeable dates. A consolidated text may be convenient for present questions but may obscure the provision governing an earlier transaction. The decision file must preserve the version applied to the relevant event and the legal reason for applying it. Where a co
-## 19.5 A machine-readable obligation model
-The smallest useful Qānūn-Map object is not a paragraph of code. It is a legal proposition whose elements and consequences can be inspected independently. For a VASP-perimeter screen, the object may be expressed as follows:
-| Element | Structured representation | Human/legal boundary |
-|---|---|---|
-| actor | identified person; legal form; role; verified entity and representative identifiers | whether multiple actors form one service or exercise control |
-| activity | described function, customer journey, asset flow, custody, interface, remuneration and jurisdiction | classification by substance, function, use and economic effect |
-| territorial condition | carried on, or held out as carried on, in or from Pakistan | targeting, representations and cross-border facts may be disputed |
-| business condition | business and professional basis | isolated activity, group allocation and commercial substance require evidence |
-| relational condition | service to third parties | principal/agent, own-account and customer relationships require legal analysis |
-| service category | section 18 and Schedule I candidate category | ambiguous or combined services require reasoned classification |
-| exception/perimeter | section 2 exclusions and SBP/SECP or other connected law | no automatic exemption; competent regulator coordination may be required |
-| current legal proposition | the Act’s scope, VASP definition, service categories and NOC/licensing provisions apply according to their terms | exact NOC, licence, unauthorised-activity or transition consequence depends on operative law and proved facts |
-| recommended administrative routing | route a potentially in-scope case to PVARA without representing that the screen proves a licence, exemption or breach | this is a safe workflow recommendation, not a new statutory duty triggered merely by screening uncertainty |
-| evidence | terms, user flow, entity records, wallet/key control, fees, transaction samples and marketing | authenticity, completeness, privilege and weight remain reviewable |
-| institution | PVARA for VAA classification; connected institution for its own statutory perimeter | coordination does not transfer statutory competence |
-| reason/remedy | cited path, missing facts, decision-maker, review and appeal route | only the competent body can make the relevant order or adjudication |
-The Virtual Assets Act supplies the principal source chain. Section 2 states the Pakistan nexus and express exclusions. Section 3 defines a VASP as a person who, as a business, provides one or more virtual-asset services to third parties on a professional basis. Section 9(1)(f) authorises PVARA to classify by substance and economic effect, with consultation where SBP or SECP characteristics appea
-These provisions contain both formal and evaluative elements. Code can check that a declared entity identifier exists, that a date has a valid format, that required evidence fields are present, that a selected service category has a source link, or that two supplied Boolean values follow a declared branch. It cannot establish, merely from an applicant’s checkbox, that an operation is “professiona
-Accordingly, an automation model should classify functions by permitted use rather than by optimism about technical capability:
-- **publication and retrieval:** source discovery, provision linking and status display;
-- **syntactic validation:** format, completeness, arithmetic, date and identifier checks;
-- **screening and routing:** candidate classification and identification of the competent human pathway;
-- **decision support:** comparison of evidence with declared criteria, with an authorised officer independently responsible for reasons and result; and
-- **prohibited automatic consequence:** refusal, licence grant or variation, sanction, freeze, tax assessment, liability finding, merits determination or appeal disposition without the human authority and process required by law.
-Some calculations may be highly determinate yet still depend on human-controlled inputs. Even a deadline calculation requires the correct triggering event, communication date, governing version and any lawful extension. The calculation can be reproducible while the legal premise is contested. The output must therefore show both the answer and the assumptions on which it rests.
-Missing information should produce a typed state, not a guessed value. `UNKNOWN` means a fact was not supplied or verified. `[GAP]` means the governing source or institutional mechanism is absent or unresolved. `[DRAFT]` means the candidate rule lacks operative status. `CONFLICT` means two apparently applicable authorities or data sources cannot be reconciled. Each state should generate the respo

+## 19.2 Baseline order: prolonged incompleteness
+**Assumption.** The VAA remains operative, NOC and transition cases continue to require administration, final regulatory modules or connected instruments arrive unevenly, and a material share of customer activity remains offshore or outside a clearly evidenced domestic permission. This is a continuation scenario, not a claim that delay will occur.
+The legal stress is produced by time. An NOC, pending application, sandbox permission, saved Ordinance-era instrument and statutory licence are different legal states. If the public register, completeness method, transition determination, appointment record and review route remain incomplete, repeated administrative practice may harden into market expectation without acquiring legal authority. Ba
+The affected interests are broader than applicants. Customers may believe that regulatory engagement equals full supervision. Compliant firms may bear higher costs than offshore competitors. Banks may either over-exclude legitimate applicants or supply access without a complete regulatory status. PVARA staff may be asked to decide under criteria not yet contained in valid instruments. A court may
+Current law is not empty during this scenario. Direct statutory duties concerning unauthorised activity, customer assets, conduct, AML/CFT, cooperation and enforcement remain relevant according to their terms.[^439] The danger is selective operability: coercive powers may be invoked before corresponding procedures, reasons and remedies work; businesses may face duties without a usable application
+The no-regret response is therefore Chapter 18’s Horizon I package: publish exact status; authenticate appointments and delegations; maintain the authoritative instruments register; verify the lawful review and investigation routes; decide section 74 continuity instrument by instrument; and state which requirements apply during transition. Government should progress only those measures for which
+**Early indicators.** The dashboard should watch the age and legal status of NOC and licence applications; number of publicly unclassified providers; frequency of banks requesting regulator confirmation; customer complaints caused by status confusion; unpublished or superseded documents still used in decisions; vacancies and unverified delegations; inability to file an appeal; and the proportion
+**Residual risk and implication.** Even a candid transition notice cannot eliminate litigation over accrued positions or the exact operation of section 70. The design implication is to preserve customer continuity while refusing legal fiction. If the baseline persists, the response is targeted amendment or a lawfully made instrument—not indefinite administrative tolerance. **Uncertainty:** neithe
+## 19.3 Regulated-market deepening
+**Assumption.** The amendment, Rules and final Regulations contemplated by Chapter 18 are substantially completed; PVARA grants activity-specific permissions; banks supply controlled account access; and supervised domestic providers begin to mediate a greater range of customer activity. +The first stress is supervisory load. A licence converts a prospective assessment into a continuing obligation to supervise ownership, governance, capital, custody, conduct, AML/CFT, technology, outsourcing and wind-down. +The second stress is multi-function concentration. An exchange may combine brokerage, custody, lending, proprietary dealing, token listing, settlement, staking and issuance support. Customer assets may support settlement exposure; proprietary trading may influence listing or execution; and group entities may shift risk beyond t
+The third stress is connected-law dependency. A PVARA permission cannot supply SBP payment or foreign-exchange authority, SECP securities authority, FBR tax treatment, provincial services-tax treatment, property title or an environmental approval. Market deepening therefore tests the joint perimeter and referral mechanism more severely than a small transitional market. A delayed decision by one i

+**Residual risk and implication.** Regulation can shift risk rather than remove it: into concentrated providers, shared infrastructure, group entities or customer belief in State guarantee. The legal design should therefore preserve resolution, portability and failure planning from the first licence. **Uncertainty:** the verified record does not establish the future number, scale, ownership or bu
+## 19.4 Stablecoin and payment stress
+**Assumption.** One or more fiat- or asset-referenced tokens become materially used by Pakistani customers for conversion, remittance, merchant settlement, savings-like balances, DeFi collateral or cross-border trade. The scenario does not assume that such use is lawful in every form, that a token is legal tender, or that adoption reaches any numerical threshold.
+Stablecoin scale compresses several legal events into a fast technical path: acquisition with rupees or foreign currency; custody or self-hosting; cross-border transfer; conversion; payment instruction; merchant settlement; reserve redemption; and accounting or tax recognition. Different institutions may own each decision. The VAA provides fiat- and asset-referenced categories and issuer/reserve
+Three failure mechanisms should be tested. First, an **issuer run** may arise from doubt about reserve quality, custody, legal title, redemption, banking access or sanctions. Secondly, a **gateway interruption** may prevent conversion or merchant settlement even where the token continues to trade on-chain. Thirdly, a **cross-border integrity shock** may cause foreign issuers, banks or platforms t
+The financial-integrity stress is substantial. FATF’s 2025 update reports increasing illicit use of stablecoins, continuing offshore-VASP challenges and weak recovery after major thefts; its revised Recommendation 16 also changes international payment-transparency expectations.[^441] These are global observations, not findings about Pakistani users. They justify a system capable of identifying or
+The monetary and prudential stress is different. BIS’s 2026 analysis recognises tokenisation’s potential while concluding that current stablecoin arrangements do not supply all foundational properties of money and may create integrity and macro-financial challenges at scale.[^442] For Pakistan, the relevant question is not whether a foreign report prefers another monetary architecture. It is whet
+Chapter 18’s FRT module should therefore be tested before material retail or payment scale. +**Early indicators.** Authorities should monitor, under lawful data powers, stablecoin exposure by provider and use rather than publicity estimates; concentration by issuer, reserve custodian and blockchain; redemption requests and delay; deviations from the promised reference; changes in issuer terms; bank or gateway interruptions; use as DeFi collateral; self-hosted and cross-border transfer pa
+**Residual risk and implication.** Pakistan cannot compel a foreign issuer, reserve bank or blockchain to continue service. Domestic rules can limit exposure, require local accountability, preserve evidence and create an exit route, but cannot guarantee parity. The legal design implication is to cap or condition retail, payment or public-sector reliance until redemption and failure tests pass, an
+## 19.5 Tokenised assets and capital-market expansion

A sandbox de
+**Early indicators.** The dashboard should record asset classes proposed; classification time; percentage of pilots with complete legal-rights memoranda; authoritative-register integration; reconciliation exceptions; corporate actions requiring manual correction; rejected or reversed transfers; custody concentration; secondary-market liquidity; investor complaints; and unresolved questions of per
+**Residual risk and implication.** Some legal rights may not be suitable for tokenisation without primary amendment or registry reform. +## 19.6 DeFi, DAO and autonomous-agent diffusion
+**Assumption.** Pakistani customers obtain material access to decentralised exchanges, lending pools, staking arrangements, DAO-governed services or AI systems that recommend, initiate or manage virtual-asset transactions. Access may occur through local interfaces, foreign applications, wallets, APIs or general-purpose agents. The scenario does not assume that a protocol is decentralised merely b
+The first stress is factual attribution. A protocol may involve developers, deployers, interface operators, governance participants, oracle providers, administrators, multisignature signers, liquidity suppliers, fee recipients and users. Their legal significance differs. IOSCO’s DeFi work treats claims of decentralisation as facts to be examined through control, influence, economic interest and o
+The second stress is authority. An automated system may form or perform a contract, route an order, rebalance assets, vote, borrow, liquidate collateral or transmit a payment. Pakistan’s Electronic Transactions Ordinance supports electronic form and attribution of automated communications to a person using or controlling the system, but attribution does not resolve consent, authority, mistake, fi
+An AI agent sharpens this problem because it may select tools and actions not individually specified by the user. A provider could describe the output as information while the system actually personalises advice, exercises discretion or executes transactions. A customer may give a broad natural-language instruction that the agent converts into a chain of swaps, approvals and protocol interactions
+The third stress is common-mode behaviour. If many firms use the same model, data source, cloud service, oracle or agent framework, apparently independent decisions may become correlated. The FSB identifies third-party concentration, market correlation, cyber risk, model risk, data quality and governance as potential financial-system vulnerabilities from AI adoption.[^447] In digital-asset market
+Chapter 18’s functional perimeter remains resilient if final rules require an **automated-system responsibility file**. It should identify the legally accountable deployer; permitted task; customer mandate; activity classification; data and model dependencies; wallet and API permissions; transaction and value limits; testing; monitoring; override and shutdown; record of prompts, policy and action
+DeFi regulation should focus on the accessible service and actual control. A local interface that selects assets, routes trades, controls fees or can suspend access may carry responsibilities even if it cannot alter the base protocol. An immutable protocol may still depend on an oracle, stablecoin, bridge, hosting layer or governance process. Conversely, writing code, holding a token or casting o
+NIST’s 2026 concept paper on software and AI-agent identity and authorisation is expressly a draft project concept, not a legal standard, but it identifies a concrete design issue: autonomous systems need distinguishable identities and bounded access to data, tools and applications.[^448] Pakistan should test agent credentials, least privilege, separation of customer accounts, revocation, transac
+**Early indicators.** Relevant signals include material customer losses involving automated execution; growth in agent-controlled wallet permissions; common model, oracle, bridge or cloud dependencies; repeated overrides; actions outside mandate; unexplained correlated trading; prompt-injection or data-poisoning events; DAO administrator-key use; governance concentration; interface delisting or s
+**Residual risk and implication.** Adaptive output cannot always be predicted or explained at transaction-level precision, and a foreign protocol may lack a reachable operator. The design implication is not a fictional electronic person. It is bounded authority, attributable deployment, observable control, intervention capacity, records and loss allocation. High-impact autonomous custody, executi
+## 19.7 Cyber, fraud or institutional-failure shock
+**Assumption.** A material event affects one or more critical providers or public institutions: compromise of signing keys; insider theft; corrupted entitlement data; cloud or telecommunications outage; bridge or oracle exploit; ransomware; coordinated fraud; reserve freeze; or absence of a lawfully authorised decision-maker during the event. The scenario is compound because digital-asset failure
+The first minutes produce an authority problem. Who can halt withdrawals, isolate a wallet, direct preservation, notify customers, obtain a court order, contact a foreign provider or decide that continued operation is unsafe? A technically capable person without lawful power may protect assets but contaminate evidence or infringe rights; a legally authorised official without keys, data or a worki
+The next phase produces a property and evidence problem. The provider must distinguish customer and house assets, valid and fraudulent instructions, on-chain and off-chain liabilities, frozen and lost assets, and recoverable and irrecoverable keys. Investigators need a preserved chain connecting system logs, wallet control, transaction data, device evidence and human decisions. Customers need acc
+Fraud may exploit the same event. FATF’s 2025 update describes increasing fraud and scam exposure, major theft, stablecoin misuse and low recovery in a significant cross-border case.[^449] These global findings do not measure Pakistan. They demonstrate why the plan must cover impersonation, false recovery services, compromised customer communications, mule accounts, dormant accounts and rapid lay
+The Chapter 18 package supplies four linked safeguards. First, the customer-asset and failure plan allows reconstruction and transfer. Secondly, the incident standard supplies severity, contacts, update duties and recovery evidence. Thirdly, the investigation SOP supplies preservation, key custody, legal process and return. Fourthly, the Tribunal and court route supplies interim relief and challe
+The exercise should run without advance notice to the operational team while protecting live systems. It should simulate unavailable senior officers, a conflicted service provider, cross-border data, a disputed customer claim and an incorrect initial indicator. The after-action record should distinguish decision, authority, evidence, elapsed time, customer impact, failed dependency and remediatio

+The heat map is a consequence comparison, not a probability map. Its central result is that the compound shock can defeat all modules simultaneously, while otherwise distinct scenarios repeatedly stress coordination and remedy. The common corrective priority is therefore a tested decision chain, not another general statement that cyber risk is important.
+**Early indicators.** Signals include privileged-access anomalies; key-policy exceptions; unresolved reconciliation breaks; vendor or cloud concentration; repeated high-severity vulnerabilities; fraudulent domain and social-media impersonation; abrupt withdrawal or complaint spikes; delayed incident classification; inconsistent public statements; unavailable decision-makers; evidence-transfer fai
+**Residual risk and implication.** No architecture prevents every theft, outage or fraud. Foreign recovery may fail, technical intervention may be unavailable, and compensation may not cover loss. The design implication is to minimise irreversible exposure, preserve lawful options and practise failure. **Uncertainty:** the initiating event, target, duration, asset-recovery rate and contagion path
+## 19.8 Cross-border fragmentation or harmonisation
+**Assumption.** Foreign jurisdictions continue to implement crypto-asset, stablecoin, tax, payment, sanctions, data and AI rules at different speeds. Some requirements converge through international standards while market-access, custody, issuer, privacy and enforcement rules remain incompatible. Pakistan may face both demands for recognition and restrictions by foreign providers.
+The scenario stresses section 4 extraterritorial reach and sections 9 and 17 cooperation and recognition powers. An offshore platform may target Pakistan without a conventional establishment; a foreign issuer may serve local wallets but deny local jurisdiction; or a Pakistan licensee may depend on a custodian whose home regulator restricts service. Two authorities may demand inconsistent retentio
+The FSB’s 2025 review identifies gaps and inconsistencies in implementation and the resulting opportunity for regulatory arbitrage.[^450] FATF’s revised Recommendation 16 increases convergence around payment-message information, but international convergence does not itself decide Pakistan’s domestic authority, privacy safeguards or technical interface.[^451] Tax reporting adds another lane: CARF
+Chapter 18’s issue-specific recognition model is robust if every reliance decision identifies the activity, comparable outcome, home supervisor, data and record access, customer-asset location, local service and complaint route, enforcement cooperation, transition and withdrawal. Recognition should reduce duplicate evidence only where cooperation works. Material retail, custody, payment or stable
+The contrary path—fragmentation—requires an exit playbook. PVARA should be able to identify affected customers, assets, dependencies and contractual rights; require notice and transfer; preserve records; coordinate with SBP, FMU, tax and enforcement bodies; and state what Pakistan can and cannot compel. An untested promise of international cooperation is not a safeguard.
+**Early indicators.** The dashboard should track foreign legal changes affecting Pakistan access; rejected supervisory requests; delayed or incomplete Travel Rule messages; foreign licence restrictions; concentration in jurisdictions without effective cooperation; conflicts over data, sanctions or freezes; sudden terms-of-service changes; blocked redemptions or withdrawals; and growing targeted s
+**Residual risk and implication.** Pakistan cannot harmonise foreign law unilaterally and should not trade away constitutional, monetary, tax or customer-protection requirements for nominal access. The design implication is selective interoperability with an executable withdrawal route. **Uncertainty:** foreign reforms, equivalence decisions, geopolitical conditions and provider cooperation are e
+## 19.9 Mining, energy and environmental pathway
+**Assumption.** Public or private actors seek to expand virtual-asset mining because of claimed surplus generation, changing tariffs, investment proposals or new equipment economics—or existing operations contract or migrate when those conditions change. PVARA may regulate a mining-related virtual-asset service, but it does not allocate power, approve a connection, set a tariff or grant environme
+The main stress is temporal mismatch. Electricity described as surplus at one hour, season or network location may have another use at a different time. A long-lived concession based on a short-lived surplus can shift grid, fuel, capacity, transmission or environmental cost to households, firms or public finance. Technology may also change the revenue per unit of energy before the State recovers
+International evidence establishes the materiality of energy and emissions, not Pakistan’s local balance. IMF analysis links crypto mining and data centres to growing electricity demand and environmental externalities and cautions against special fiscal treatment without accounting for grid and social cost.[^452] Its global estimates and proposed tax rates are not transplanted into Pakistani law
+Chapter 18’s approval stack should govern every project: verified load and location; generation and transmission evidence; lawful connection and tariff; curtailment priority; metering; environmental screening and approval; water and equipment-disposal effects where material; land and local permission; tax and customs treatment; procurement or allocation authority; public-money control; employment
+**Early indicators.** Relevant signals are requested and connected load; hourly and seasonal utilisation; curtailment and grid congestion; tariff recovery and arrears; fuel and foreign-exchange exposure; emissions and environmental non-compliance; water or equipment-waste impacts; fiscal incentives; public infrastructure cost; jobs and local expenditure actually delivered; unauthorised mining; an
+**Residual risk and implication.** Even a compliant project may become uneconomic or impose opportunity costs when energy conditions change. The design implication is a reversible, measured permission—not a strategic entitlement. **Uncertainty:** future mining technology, asset economics, energy mix, location and genuinely available surplus are unknown; no public return is forecast.
+## 19.10 Rights and distribution under the scenarios
+None of the scenarios is distributionally neutral. The same control can protect one interest and burden another. Enhanced traceability may reduce fraud but expose financial associations; a rapid freeze may preserve assets but restrict innocent property; high capital requirements may protect customers but concentrate the market; local-presence rules may improve remedy but exclude a useful foreign
+The constitutional frame remains legality, fair treatment, privacy and dignity, economic freedom subject to law, property, equality, information, federal distribution of authority and effective judicial review. These rights do not decide every policy outcome, but they require lawful source, rational classification, proportionality where rights are restricted, reasons and remedy.[^453]

+The rights test must occur at design and incident stages. A lawful data field can become disproportionate when retained indefinitely or shared for a new purpose. An emergency restriction can become unlawful when urgency ends. An algorithmic risk score can support triage but should not become an undisclosed reason for licence refusal, account closure or enforcement. Human review must have authorit
+Distribution should also be measured by who can exit. A sophisticated institution may diversify custodians, verify reserves and litigate abroad; a retail user may rely on a phone interface and regulatory badge. Chapter 18’s portability, reasons and remedy controls therefore protect capability, not merely formal equality. The National Digital Masterplan framework can coordinate inclusion and infra
+**Cross-scenario implication.** The dashboard should disaggregate complaints, losses, freezes, service interruptions, licensing outcomes and remediation where lawful and statistically responsible. It should test whether burdens cluster by customer type, region, gender, disability, business size or access channel without turning protected data into a new risk. **Uncertainty:** distributional effec
